Declared (not equivalent, kept on purpose):

- **Set-order messages.** When a batch's event tuples cannot be sorted, which
  pair the reference compares first depends on the iteration order of a
  Python set: random across hash seeds when the tuples hold strings, and
  otherwise fixed by CPython's hash-table layout, which native does not
  model. Both raise a TypeError; native's message names a pair the inputs
  hold, and the test accepts either operand order.
- **NaN object identity.** An object column holding the same NaN object
  (`np.nan` written into several cells) dedupes those event ids in the
  reference; native reads cells from files, where every NaN is its own value,
  as the reference treats float64 columns and separately created NaNs.
- **None event id label.** A None event id is listed as the text `None` in the
  native batch event, where the reference tuple holds None.
- **Equal mixed-type case ids in one batch.** When `0` and `0.0` are case ids
  of events merged into one batch, which of the two equal values the
  reference reports is deterministic but not modeled; membership and counts
  agree.
- Two Woflan inputs fail inside the reference runtime (`nx_utils.topological_sort`
  is missing); they are reference failures, not expectations. The weighted
  Woflan analysis, the 65572296 and 61ebeee0 declarations and the earlier DC4,
  C3, streaming and Windows declarations stay in force.

  depends on the iteration order of a Python set and, with NaN ids, on
  object identity: over 40 hash seeds the same input names different pairs
  (or `boolean value of NA is ambiguous`) and some inputs even succeed under
  one seed and raise under another (the reviewer's five qualified message
  cases are of this kind, and native's message is among the reference's).
  The test lists every observed result and accepts any. Two of the 1,400
  fuzz tables are the remaining layout case: the tuples whose comparison
  fails first hold no strings or NaN, so CPython's hash-table layout puts
  them first under every seed, while native sorts the set in insertion order
  and names another failing pair of the same inputs; both raise TypeError
  (`DECLARED set-layout` in the fixture).
- **NaN object identity in object columns.** An object column holding one NaN
  object in several cells dedupes those event ids in the reference; native
  reads cells from files, where every NaN is its own value (the reference's
  float64 columns and separately created NaNs agree, and "str" columns now
  share their NaN as the reference does).
- **None labels.** A None event id is listed as the text `None` and a None case
  id in an object column as `nan` in native batch events, where the reference
  tuple holds None.
- **Equal mixed-type representatives** are no longer declared: the merge
  model above reports the reference's value for case and event ids (1,000
  fuzz tables, all representatives equal).
- MSVC is not available in the cloud container; the Windows CI job is the
  build check. Earlier declarations (c8ee22d, 65572296, 61ebeee0, DC4, C3,
  streaming, Windows) stay in force.

## Recheck of 7270a1f: fixes and declarations (2026-10-28)

The recheck of 7270a1f reported four targets (O1-O4). The reviewer's handoff
was on a machine that was offline during this round, so each target was found
from its title against public PM4Py 2.7.22 calls (pandas 3.0.5, numpy 2.4.6)
and fuzzed until native and reference agreed. The fuzz covered 1,200 grouping
tables with NaN, None, pd.NA, NaT, infinities and huge integers in object and
float64 key columns next to typed columns, and 2,000 grouping tables over two
typed key columns of every numpy and masked numeric dtype. It also covered
10,000 tables for the other pandas sequence and case filters over typed case
and activity columns (numpy, masked and mixed object), 624 fixed probes, and
4,000 PNML models with toolspecifics of many tools, tags and namespaces.
`minera_recheck_7270a1f_tests` binds all of them with their saved reference
results (`src/backend/tests/fixtures/recheck_7270a1f/`, written by
`scripts/generate-recheck-7270a1f-fixture.py` from
`scripts/capture-recheck-7270a1f-reference.py` output).

Once the handoff could be read (2026-10-31), the reviewer's cases were
replayed against 46d14cd and bound into the same test with their saved public
results. These are the 100 grouping tables of
`filtering-statistics/a7270-cases.json` (every focused O1/O2 fixture among
them, the two qualified Float32/null tables included), all of which match.
They also include the 75 eligible PNML captures of
`discovery-conformance/p7*-pnml-properties-reference.jsonl` (the six O3/O4
manifestations and their controls), read the way the reviewer's CLI comparison
reads them. Of those, 71 match and four are the declared priority-range and
Unicode 14 cases. The reviewer excluded eight captures because their harness
converted a None getter result itself. Those models were captured again
without that conversion and match too: an omitted weight or priority and an
empty or untyped block import cleanly, while an empty priority, a nested-before
weight, an omitted exponential parameter and an empty weight raise
TypeError inside the importer.

| ID | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| O1 | Consecutive activity/case grouping adds two numeric key columns in numpy's result type. bool joins the other side (bool + bool stays bool). Integers of one signedness take the wider width and wrap in it. A signed and an unsigned integer take the next signed width that holds both (float64 past 64 bits). A float side takes the narrowest float that holds both (an 8-bit integer fits float16, a 16-bit one float32), rounding to that width. A masked side makes the key masked, and an NA cell makes the key NA. Runs compare the key with its shifted copy: integer keys as float64, float keys in their own width (NaN never equal), bool keys exactly, and an NA comparison starts no run. Next to an object column, a masked column adds the value stored under its mask (an int of IntN/UIntN, NaN of FloatN, a bool of boolean). The retry after a TypeError uses those values too, and the key is NA where either side is missing. | same (`fuzz-dtypes`, 2,000 tables) |
| O2 | Object run keys add over every row, missing cells included, and retry the present rows only after a TypeError. A NaN, None, pd.NA or NaT that meets an int too large for a float therefore raises `OverflowError: int too large to convert to float`, unless a TypeError comes first. | same (`fuzz-run-keys`, 1,200 tables) |
| O3 | PNML transitions read toolspecifics as PM4Py does: any tag ending in `toolspecific` (namespaced or not, case-sensitive). A tool containing `ProM` may mark the transition invisible (activity containing `$invisible$`). Otherwise a tool containing `StochasticPetriNet` starts a new stochastic record that replaces the previous one, and any keyed child element is a property, where a later key replaces an earlier one. Other tools are ignored together with their properties. A missing tool or ProM activity attribute raises PM4Py's `argument of type 'NoneType' is not a container or iterable`. | same (`pnml-cases.tsv.gz`, 4,000 models, with and without the map) |
| O4 | Only the exact type names IMMEDIATE, DETERMINISTIC, NORMAL, UNIFORM, LOGNORMAL, GAMMA and EXPONENTIAL define a random variable. Any other type, or none, is an undefined variable and keeps the native default record. IMMEDIATE ignores parameters. DETERMINISTIC keeps the text. NORMAL and UNIFORM take the first two `;` parts (None raises `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'split'`; one part raises `list index out of range`). LOGNORMAL and GAMMA convert three parts with `float()` in order, with its message. EXPONENTIAL converts the whole text: 0 raises `division by zero` and a non-positive rate is undefined. The writer emits two parameters for NORMAL/UNIFORM and three for LOGNORMAL/GAMMA. A PNML map is checked structurally on import and export; distribution domains are checked where the map is used. | same |
| O1+ | The same dtype rules in the other pandas filters. Grouping by a float16 column raises `NotImplementedError: float16 indexes are not supported` (rework, prefix/suffix, case size, variants, start/end/nocc, timestamp grouping). first/last aggregations raise `agg function failed [how->first|last,dtype->D]` with pandas' D. A wrapping int64 progression of case ids makes set_index raise `Length mismatch`. The activity split orders case ids as np.unique does (NaN last, all NaNs one run) and labels them with numpy's str of the scalar (shortest round-trip digits in float16/float32/float64 width). `==` filters cast a number to a float16/float32 column's width, while isin compares exactly. A missing start/end activity is None, NaN or pd.NA by dtype (matched by None, NaN or nothing). nocc counts the missing boundaries of float and masked columns separately. Variant joins raise `sequence item j: expected str instance, T found` with Python or numpy type names, and admitted patterns are read only when a case exists. | same (`fuzz-typed` case/activity/mixed, 10,000 tables; `typed-probes`, 624) |

Declared (not equivalent, kept on purpose):

- **Finite stochastic values.** A native stochastic map holds finite numbers,
  finite non-negative activation weights and priorities that fit an int.
  PM4Py keeps DETERMINISTIC, NORMAL and UNIFORM parameter text it never
  converts, infinite and NaN values, an `UNDEFINED` exponential mean, any float
  weight and any Python int priority. Native imports those models without
  the map unchanged, and with the map raises a policy error. The fixture marks
  these 289 models `POLICY`.
- **Undefined random variables and absent weight/priority** keep the native
  default record (exponential timing, weight 1, priority 0). PM4Py holds an
  undefined variable with no parameters.
- **GAMMA and LOGNORMAL parameters** are kept by position (first, second and
  third value), as PM4Py reads them. Their meaning in native sampling is the
  native one.
- **PNML text quirks** that the public importer shows only through lxml
  (processing instructions inside property text, tag suffix matching across
  namespaces) are covered as far as the 4,000 fuzz models reach and not
  modelled beyond that.
- **uint64 type names.** numpy names a UInt64 activity `numpy.uint64` or
  `numpy.ulonglong` depending on which values the process converted before.
  Native names `ulonglong` when every value lies past the int64 range, which
  is what a fresh process reports, and the capture reruns such cases in a
  fresh process.
- **Unicode 14 digits.** Native number parsing uses Unicode 14 tables, so
  digits added later (Kawi) do not convert natively, while the reviewer's
  Python 3.14 (Unicode 16) accepts them. These are two of the reviewer's PNML
  captures.
- Earlier declarations (d5b33ef, c8ee22d, 65572296, 61ebeee0, DC4, C3,
  streaming, Windows) stay in force.

## Stream sessions: CSV rows, TBR termination counts and session limits (2026-11-01)

- **CSV stream rows.** The reference CSV event stream reader (csv.DictReader)
  keeps every row in file order, so an empty or pandas-NA-spelled case id or
  activity (`NA`, `null`, `NaN`, ...) is literal text there. The batch
  importer still drops those rows like read_csv/format_dataframe;
  `CsvImportOptions::keep_na_first_class_values` keeps them, and the CSV
  event stream reader (now in file order), live-session batches, reader
  sessions and the one-shot streaming routes set it. Tests:
  `minera_streaming_import_tests` (`csv_events_keep_na_spellings_in_file_order`).
- **Streaming TBR termination counts.** The forward variant now reports the
  reference's signed sums: missing adds `final - marking` over the final
  places and remaining is `sum(marking) - sum(final)`, so `[A]` on
  `p0-A->p1-B->p2` ends with missing 1, remaining 0 and a surplus sink token
  lowers missing. A marking equal to the final one apart from zero-token keys
  is fit, as in the reference (the earlier zero-key rule was wrong; the
  9258a44 bank compared only fitness). All 39 bank cases now also check
  missing/remaining. Backwards replay has no reference counterpart and keeps
  per-place counts. Tests: `minera_streaming_tbr_tests`.
- **Live sessions.** Events are counted without copying the DFG per event,
  queues drain without holding the session lock (a snapshot with
  `wait_until_drained=false`, list and release no longer wait for a drain),
  responses list the latest 1000 deliveries (`deliveries_limit`, at most
  100000) with `deliveries_offset`, and each registry (live, reader,
  acquisition) holds at most 32 sessions (429 beyond), with 256 MiB of
  uploads and 1,000,000 events per live session (413 beyond). Tests:
  `minera_streaming_session_tests`.
- **Stream session limits (declared native limits).** The reference streams
  without bounds; the server declares these:
  - Per live session: 256 MiB of uploads and 1,000,000 events. A batch is
    refused (413) before parsing when its estimate would pass the limit, and
    again after parsing on the exact count.
  - Per reader session: 1,000,000 events, estimated before parsing. A CSV
    source counts its non-blank rows after the header; an XES source counts
    its `<event` start tags within `xes_max_traces` traces. A source
    estimated above the limit gets 413, so a source with exactly 1,000,000
    rows is accepted.
  - Server-wide: 1 GiB of source bytes and 2,000,000 events across all live
    and reader sessions (429 beyond). A reader is charged once, for its
    source bytes and its estimated events. The session lists report the
    budget in use as `stream_budget` (`bytes`, `events`, `max_bytes`,
    `max_events`).
  - Idle expiry: a live or reader session that no request names (create,
    snapshot, read, append, action, source, export, release; the session
    lists do not count) for 30 minutes is released as an explicit release
    would be, and its budget returned. A session still working through
    queued events (`ACTIVE` with `pending` events) is never expired, and each
    request or append restarts its idle time. A request for an expired
    session gets 404 ("expired after being idle"). `MINERA_STREAM_IDLE_MS`
    overrides the expiry in milliseconds; 0 disables it.
  - The frontend keeps its live or reader session when the user moves to
    another view, so a running stream survives and the remembered id
    reconnects to it. It releases the session when the user replaces it
    ("Release and start a separate …", or a new session or reader source).
  Tests: `minera_server_parameter_contract_tests` (1,000,001 rows refused
  with an exact estimate, LF and CRLF with blank lines; idle expiry on a
  server with a 1.5 s expiry).
- **Mining admission and memory (declared native limits).** The reference
  mines whatever it is given; the server declares these:
  - Size cap: `/api/mine` counts CSV rows or XES `<event` tags before
    parsing and estimates 10 KiB per event plus 2 KiB per event for each
    column beyond case, activity, timestamp and resource. Above the budget
    (half the physical or cgroup memory; `--mine-memory-budget`) or
    `--max-mine-events` it answers 413 `MINE_LIMIT` with the estimate, the
    limit and a hint. Sampling does not lift it: the whole upload is
    retained as the source.
  - One `/api/mine` at a time; others get 503 `MINE_BUSY` with
    `Retry-After` (1 s when the running mine is already canceled, else 5 s).
  - A canceled or replaced mine stops between stages with the existing
    canceled 400 instead of running to completion; results of a mine that
    is not canceled are byte-identical.
  - Memory: the session shares the active source's checked log instead of
    copying it, and shares a prepared Alpha or Inductive log that came out
    unchanged; the source's stream and lazy table views are built on first
    use; the upload is parsed in place and the response tail is written in
    place. On a 200,000-event, four-column CSV the mine's peak RSS fell from
    3.44 GB to 1.59 GB and its retained (trimmed) RSS from 2.61 GB to
    0.88 GB, with a byte-identical 122,914,698-byte response.
  - With zlib, JSON and text responses are gzipped on `Accept-Encoding:
    gzip` (never a 206 range); the mining body shrinks about tenfold.
  Tests: `minera_server_parameter_contract_tests` (gzip round trip with
  exact bytes for a repaired body and for `/api/mine`, Range with gzip, 415
  for a gzip request body; 413 for the budget and the event cap; 503 while
  a mine runs; cancel between stages on a server with
  `MINERA_MINE_STAGE_PAUSE_MS`), `mine-admission.test.ts`.

## BPMN, transition systems, performance spectrum and sampling (2026-11-03)

Fixes:

- **Multiset transition systems.** The reference looks a state up by its
  Counter value among the states registered so far (both endpoints are looked
  up before either is registered), keeps one root state per name and dedups
  edges by endpoint values and label. Native now does the same, and when two
  equal-valued states exist (reached under different key orders) a later
  lookup takes the first-registered one, where the reference's choice depends
  on set iteration. `A,B,A` backward (window 2) has 3 states with an
  `{A,B} -A-> {A,B}` self-loop and `d,a,d,c` backward has 4 states, as in
  the reference. Tests: `minera_transition_system_parity_contracts_tests`
  (`transition_system_multiset_value_lookup_contract`).
- **Performance spectrum.** A pattern activity that never occurs yields no
  observations (the reference's empty points list) instead of a "not
  registered" error. Test: `minera_performance_spectrum_cli_missing_activity`.
- **BPMN import.** Processes that use only start and end events, task kinds
  (not call activities), exclusive and parallel gateways are converted with
  the reference construction: `source`/`sink`, `ent_<id>`/`exi_<id>` per
  node, one place per sequence flow named by its id, `sfl_`/`tfl_` silent
  connectors, a forking/joining silent transition for parallel gateways with
  several outgoing/incoming flows, start/end connectors, then the reference's
  two-pass simple reduction of silent connectors. Place names and transition
  names are carried on the net (PNML export uses the place names). Dangling
  gateways, isolated tasks, a task with several outgoing flows (an exclusive
  choice there) and processes without start or end events are accepted as in
  the reference. Comparison against `convert_to_petri_net(read_bpmn(...))` on
  618 inputs (18 hand-written, 600 random): 514 equal in places, labels, arcs
  and markings, 1 rejected by both, and 103 declared below (97 silent cycles,
  6 constructs outside the reference converter). Tests: `minera_bpmn_reference_parity_tests` (21 captured nets).
- **Petri-net BPMN export.** Uses the reference mapping: an exclusive gateway
  per place, start event into the source gateway and the sink gateway into the
  end event, one task per visible transition (equally labelled transitions
  keep separate tasks, as in the reference; until 2026-11-03 native shared
  one task per label, which differed on 101 of 199 seeded nets and gave the
  shared task several outgoing flows, which BPMN starts all at once) with a
  converging parallel gateway for several input places
  and a diverging one for several output places (an exclusive gateway on a
  side with no place), a silent transition as one parallel gateway when it
  has several input or output places (Converging when several inputs) and an
  exclusive gateway otherwise, then the removal of exclusive gateways with one
  incoming and one outgoing flow, so dangling places keep their gateways.
  135 alpha/heuristic/inductive nets (3 x 15 random trees) are isomorphic to
  the reference's export including gateway directions; the inductive-tree
  export is isomorphic on 26 of 26 logs it could be checked on (two larger
  logs ran out of memory in the full CLI bundle, unrelated to BPMN).
  Fresh file-level comparison (2026-11-03) against
  `write_bpmn(convert_to_bpmn(net), auto_layout=False)`: 199 of 199 seeded
  nets (tree-derived and random, many with duplicate labels) give the same
  multiset of nodes (kind, task name, gateway direction) and labelled flows;
  `minera_bpmn_reference_parity_tests` adds four captured duplicate-label
  nets. Declared: for one net that is not a workflow net the reference
  raises "Unsupported conversion of the provided object to BPMN"; native
  exports any accepting net.
- **Process-tree BPMN export.** The block-by-block export matches the
  reference export file on 600 seeded trees (sequence, xor, parallel, loop,
  or) except where the reference converter drops a flow: it loses the exit
  flow of a sequence with one child (`X(->(a), c)` leaves task `a` without
  an outgoing flow, `->(->(a, b))` leaves the end event unreached), 61 of
  600. Native keeps the flow, so its document stays connected (declared).
- **Exported BPMN documents.** Gateways carry `gatewayDirection`, every node
  lists `<incoming>`/`<outgoing>`, events are named `start`/`end`, and a
  `BPMNDiagram` with a deterministic layered layout (longest-path columns,
  back edges ignored) is included. bpmn-moddle 9.0.1 reads every checked
  export without warnings with a shape per node and an edge per flow; the
  reference importer and the native importer both read the exports, and on
  163 round trips the language equals the reference export's round trip.
  Token replay and alignment fitness on reference-converted BPMN models
  matched in 21 of 21 checked logs.
- **Sampling.** `sample_cases` and `sample_events` are a filter step that runs
  first (`LogFilterOptions::sampling`): `/api/mine` fields `sample_cases`,
  `sample_events`, `sample_seed` (alias `seed`), `sample_input`; CLI
  `--sample-cases`, `--sample-events`, `--sample-seed`, `--sample-input`.
  Native has its own MT19937 with CPython's `random.seed` (init_by_array over
  the seed's 32-bit words), `getrandbits`, `_randbelow`, `shuffle` and
  `sample` (pool or selection-set method by CPython's set-size rule) and
  numpy's legacy `RandomState` seeding, masked `interval` and `permutation`.
  `sample_input=dataframe` (the default, as `pm4py.read_xes` and a pandas CSV
  read give a DataFrame) follows `sample_cases(df, n)`: shuffle of the
  distinct case ids in row order, then the points-subset picker (indices 0 and
  len-1 plus `(j*n)//m + n//(2m)`), rows kept in original order; and
  `sample_events(df, n)` = `df.sample(n)` = the first n of a numpy
  permutation. `event_log` follows `random.sample` over the traces for both
  calls (the reference's `sample_events` on an EventLog samples traces), and
  `event_stream` follows `random.sample` over the flattened events. Seeded
  runs reproduce the reference after `random.seed(s); numpy.random.seed(s)`
  exactly. Tests: `minera_sampling_tests` (captures of CPython 3.11, numpy
  and pm4py on four seeds, the picker on 45 sizes),
  `minera_sampling_filters_cli_seeded_cases`.

Declarations:

- **Unseeded sampling.** Without a seed native draws one from the OS
  cryptographic source and reports it (`"sampling":{...,"seed":s}` in the
  mining response, a `note:` line on the CLI), so the run can be replayed;
  the reference's unseeded generators are not reproducible either. Seeds are
  limited to 0..4294967295 (numpy's legacy seeding range, used for both
  generators).
- **Sampling edge cases.** Negative counts are rejected (the reference's
  `random.sample` raises; its DataFrame `sample_cases` treats them like 0).
  An empty table samples to an empty log where the reference raises
  IndexError. A DataFrame `sample_events` above the row count is rejected as
  in pandas; the other inputs clamp to the population as the reference does.
  `sample_cases` on an event stream is rejected (not defined there).
- **Regrouping sampled events.** A log needs traces, so sampled events are
  regrouped: traces in the order their first event was sampled, events of a
  trace in their original order (the order the reference's table algorithms
  restore by sorting on case and timestamp). The reference returns rows or
  stream events in sample order. A DataFrame sample never keeps traces
  without events (they have no rows), as in the reference.
- **Multi-pool BPMN.** Native reads the first non-empty `<process>`; the
  reference merges the nodes and flows of every process into one graph.
- **BPMN silent cycles.** When the raw construction has a cycle of silent
  connectors, the reference's reduction merges a transition into itself and
  leaves arcs pointing at removed nodes; native skips that merge, so the net
  stays well-formed and differs there (97 of the 600 random inputs; all 97
  reference nets have dangling arcs).
- **BPMN constructs outside the reference converter.** Intermediate events,
  event-based, inclusive and complex gateways, subprocesses, boundary events
  and call activities keep native's token-semantics mapping: the reference
  treats them as plain nodes (wrong semantics) or fails (call activities,
  complex gateways, transactions crash its reader).
- **BPMN connector names.** Reference connector transitions get random
  UUIDs; native names them `00000000-0000-4000-8000-<counter>`.
- **Footprints of loops with more than two children.** The reference
  process-tree footprints read only a loop's first two children; a later
  redo child contributes its activities and nothing else (`*(->(c,a),c,d)`
  has no `(a,d)` or `(d,c)` sequence, and `d` is never a start or end
  activity), although the reference's own Petri-net conversion makes it an
  alternative redo. Native footprints follow the n-ary loop semantics used by
  every native conversion (body, then any redo child), so they describe the
  model's language (90 of 2,000 seeded trees with three-child loops differ,
  none without them).
- **Reachability graphs on unbounded nets.** Native stops with an error once
  the state space grows past its bound; the reference's construction does not
  terminate.

## Trie, OCEL readers, passed time and eventually-follows (2026-11-03)

Fixes:

- **Trie child order.** `log_to_trie` children keep the order in which their
  labels are first seen, walking the traces in log order (the reference
  appends a child the first time its label occurs); native sorted them by
  name. Variants CAB, B, CB, AC, CA give `[C[A*[B*],B*],B*,A[C*]]`. Fresh
  comparison: 0/200 random logs differ (CLI `--trie`, `GET /api/trie`).
  Test: `minera_trie_tests` (`reference_first_seen_order`).
- **Passed-time row order.** PRE/POST rows follow the first occurrence of
  each directly-follows pair in log order, as the reference's rows do; native
  sorted them by activity. Values, frequencies and weighted averages were
  already equal. Fresh comparison: 0/148 random logs differ. Test:
  `minera_passed_time_tests` (`reference_first_seen_order`).
- **OCEL readers drop unrelated events and objects** (OC7 above).
- **Interval eventually-follows.** The eventually-follows statistic takes the
  reference's start-timestamp key (`statistics.eventually_follows` with
  `start_timestamp_key`): each trace is stably sorted by the start attribute
  and position pair i < j counts only when event j starts at or after event i
  completes. CLI `--eventually-follows-start-attribute <name>` (and
  `--eventually-follows-timestamp-attribute`), `/api/mine` fields
  `eventually_follows_start_attribute` and
  `eventually_follows_timestamp_attribute`. A missing or unreadable start
  raises (the reference raises KeyError). Without a start attribute the
  statistic keeps every position pair i < j in trace order. Fresh comparison:
  0/80 random interval logs differ. Test: `minera_overlap_tests`
  (`eventually_follows_interval_reference`).
- **SNA with no connections.** Every reference SNA variant raises
  `ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has no
  identity` when it finds no connection (a single event, one resource for
  working together, joint activities or subcontracting, no handover). Native
  returns the empty network with `diagnostics.computed=false` and that error
  as the message, as for other reference exceptions with a computed flag
  (EMD). All 8 variants match on 158 random logs, the empty cases included.

Declarations:

- **Trie to Petri net keeps every root branch.** The reference converter
  (`objects.conversion.trie`) converts only the subtree of the root's first
  child (first-seen order), so the net's language is exactly the variants
  that start with that label (300/300 probes): `AB, CD, EF` gives a net that
  accepts only `AB`. That loses behaviour, so native keeps the full
  conversion (every root branch, shared prefix places, silent exits for
  final nodes with children, which match the reference), as for BPMN
  interleaving.
- **Reference exceptions without a computed flag.** Native keeps a result
  where the reference raises:
  - `get_log_traces_to_activities` raises `TypeError: string indices must be
    integers` whenever a sublog would be non-empty (it returns two empty lists
    only when no trace qualifies, which native matches); native returns the
    activity-targeted sublogs.
  - `filter_ocel_objects` with `level >= 2` raises `KeyError(<id>)` for an id
    that is not an object of the log (after the reader drop, an id of an
    unlinked object too); native ignores the unknown id.
  - `filter_ocel_event_attribute` and `filter_ocel_object_attribute` raise
    `KeyError(<key>)` when no event (object) carries the attribute; native
    filters with no match.
  - `read_ocel2_xml` raises `AttributeError` on a log with no event-object
    relation; native reads it as empty, like the reference JSON readers (OC7).
  - Social-network analysis and roles discovery raise when some events lack
    `org:resource`: the EventLog variants with `KeyError`, and the pandas
    handover, subcontracting and working-together variants with `TypeError`
    from sorting a string against NaN (pandas joint activities and pandas
    roles do compute, and native matches them). Native skips the events
    without a resource and returns the network or roles of the rest (trace
    a/R1, b/none, c/R2 gives the handover R1 to R2).
  - Pandas roles discovery on a log with no traces raises
    `KeyError: 'org:resource'`; native returns no roles.
  - `filter_ocel_object_types_allowed_activities` on an OCEL with no
    event-object relation raises `UFuncTypeError`; native returns an empty
    OCEL.
  - Process-tree footprints (`footprints.tree.variants.bottomup`) raise
    `KeyError(<tree>)` for many trees that repeat an activity or a subtree
    in some arrangements (`+(X(a), a)`, `*(+(c,b,a), *(b,b))`) and for every
    tree with an interleaving node (`<>(a)`): 509 of 2,000 seeded trees with
    binary loops, 747 of 2,000 with or and interleaving nodes. Native
    computes the footprints; where the reference computes, the two agree
    (0 value diffs in those 4,000).
- **Writers stay lossless.** The reference writers (JSON, XML, SQLite, CSV)
  drop unrelated events and objects, also from the OCEL in memory, before
  writing. Native writers keep what the OCEL holds, because native adapters
  use classic JSON as transport; reading such a file back through a native
  JSON, XML or SQLite reader drops them as the reference reader would, while
  a native CSV round trip keeps them (the reference's CSV round trip loses
  them at the writer). An OCEL CSV import keeps unrelated entries like the
  reference CSV reader, and they stay through every later route: a native
  OCEL JSON (both formats) that holds unrelated entries carries
  `"minera:keepUnrelated": true`, and the JSON reader keeps them when it sees
  that marker (OC8). Files without the marker are read as the reference
  reader reads them.
- **Eventually-follows without a start attribute** counted pairs in trace
  order; the reference first sorts each trace by completion timestamp. This
  only differed on XES traces whose events are not in time order. Fixed
  since: native sorts too (see "Eventually-follows sorts each case by
  timestamp").

## Seeded random modules: draws, envelopes and declarations (2026-11-03)

A review of every module whose output is random. Each contract below is
marked **exact** (draw for draw under the reference seeding, pinned by a
bank), **invariant-only** (the reference process and envelope, validated by
distribution or by invariants, because the reference draws are not
reproducible) or **declared** (a Minera extension).

All seeded draws now go through one module, `include/minera/random.hpp` /
`src/backend/random.cpp` (namespace `minera::rng`): the single MT19937
(`init_genrand` and `init_by_array` seeding), `PythonRandom` (CPython's
`random.Random`: `getrandbits`, bit-length rejection behind
`randrange`/`randint`/`choice`, `random()`, `shuffle`, `sample`),
`NumpyRandomState` (numpy's legacy `RandomState`: `random_sample`, masked
integers, `permutation`, polar normal with its cached value, exponential,
Laplace, gamma, triangular, `choice` with `p`) and portable native draws
over standard engines (`below`, `uniform_int`, `unit`, `bernoulli`,
`weighted_index`, `shuffle`, `exponential`, `normal`, `lognormal`, `gamma`).
No seeded path uses a standard-library distribution or `std::shuffle`, whose
algorithms the C++ standard leaves to the implementation; the former copies
(`src/backend/python_random.hpp`, `src/backend/numpy_legacy_random.hpp`, the
k-means++ sampler in clustering) are gone. Native-only seeded outputs that
changed with this (Petri stochastic and extensive branching, the native
Monte Carlo mode, the genetic miner, Declare playout, OCPN and OC causal-net
branching caps) are invariant-only and declared; they are now the same on
every platform. `minera_generate_sample` spells out the integer method that
produced `data/sample_event_log.csv` and still reproduces it byte for byte.
Unseeded draws (`std::random_device`) are unchanged.

- **Process-tree playout TOPBOTTOM (default): exact.** `random.seed(seed)`
  draws: `X` picks a child with `randbelow`; `*` repeats its redo child while
  `random() < 0.5`; `<>` shuffles its children in place, and the shuffled
  order persists for later traces of the same call; `+` shuffles an index list
  per element and merges. OR raises (the reference raises TypeError). The log
  has no case id and no timestamp. Bank: `scripts/capture-process-tree-
  topbottom-bank.py` (300 trees, seeds 0-2, PYTHONHASHSEED 0-2 identical,
  900 cases) drives `minera_process_tree_topbottom_parity_tests`. The former
  loop cap is an explicit opt-in (`cap_sampled_loops`,
  `playout_cap_sampled_loops`); `max_steps` is a safety bound that raises.
- **Process-tree playout BASIC_PLAYOUT: invariant-only.** The reference walks
  a set of enabled vertices (identity order), so only the process is matched:
  a uniform pick among enabled vertices, a loop choosing redo or exit with
  `randint(1, 2)` (a two-child loop exits through an implicit silent step),
  OR selecting each child with `random() < 0.5` (none selected: an empty
  trace), interleaving shuffling its children and running them in sequence.
  Envelope: cases `"0"`, `"1"`, ... and timestamps from epoch 10,000,000,
  one second per event, counting on across cases. The distribution over 12
  trees (40,000 pooled reference traces each,
  `scripts/capture-process-tree-basic-distribution.py`) is compared with a
  chi-squared homogeneity test at 0.1% in `minera_process_tree_playout_tests`.
- **Petri BASIC_PLAYOUT: invariant-only.** The reference chooses from a set of
  transition objects. Matched process: a case stops at `maxTraceLength`
  (`max_steps`, default 1000) visible events, at a deadlock, or by a "stop"
  option that is one more equally likely choice in an accepted final marking
  (exact, or covering it with `fm_leq_accepted`), so a case at the final
  marking with n enabled transitions stops with probability 1/(n+1);
  transitions without input places are always enabled. With
  `add_only_if_fm_is_reached` rejected cases are discarded and sampling goes
  on until `noTraces` are accepted, unless none of the first `noTraces`
  attempts was accepted, in which case the log is empty (observed:
  P(empty) = (1-p)^n). Envelope: accepted cases `"0"`, `"1"`, ... and
  timestamps from epoch 10,000,000, one second per event across the returned
  cases. Declared: supplying `start`, `case_interval` or `event_interval`
  (server, CLI, workbench JSON) switches to the former `case_N` envelope
  (`add_envelope`); `max_firings_per_trace` (silent livelock) and
  `max_attempts` (the server sets 100 × traces + 1000) raise where the
  reference would not return.
- **Process-tree generator BASIC and PTANDLOGGENERATOR: exact**, labels
  included (BASIC: six characters from A-Z0-9 by `randbelow(36)`;
  PTANDLOGGENERATOR: `a`..`z`, `aa`, ... in creation order, the activity count
  from one numpy `random_sample` through the triangular inverse CDF and
  Python's half-even rounding, then `random.random()` operator, side, leaf,
  silent and duplicate draws). A duplicate phase with no other label raises
  as the reference does (IndexError). Caller-supplied BASIC activities are
  declared. Bank: `scripts/capture-random-tree-bank.py` drives
  `minera_random_tree_parity_tests`.
- **DFG playout PERFORMANCE: exact** under `numpy.random.seed(seed)` (seed
  below 2^32): the case clock starts at 10,000,000 and adds the rate once
  before each case, as a running floating-point sum (not 10,000,000 +
  (i+1) × rate, which rounds differently for rates such as 0.3 or 1e-7; the
  bank includes 0.3, 1e-7 and 86400.5); one `choice` over
  the start activities in their dict order (first occurrence in the log:
  `start_activity_order`), then per step a `choice` over the successors in
  DFG order (sorted pairs, as a DataFrame discovery gives them) with the end
  weight appended; a non-zero mean d adds d × `standard_exponential`;
  timestamps are rounded half-even to the microsecond. Bank:
  `scripts/capture-dfg-performance-playout-bank.py` (300 DFGs, PYTHONHASHSEED
  0-2 identical) drives `minera_dfg_performance_playout_parity_tests`.
  Declared: `max_events_per_trace` (counted in `truncated_traces`) and an
  explicit `start_time`. **CLASSIC envelope:** cases `"0"`.., epoch
  10,000,000, one second per event across cases.
- **split_train_test: exact** for both reference inputs
  (`SplitTrainTestInput`, `--split-input`, server `split_input`): EventLog
  (`random.shuffle`, then the first min(n, floor(n p) + 1) traces train) and
  DataFrame (the default: one `random() <= p` per case in order of
  appearance, rows keep their order). Pinned by exact outcomes in
  `minera_log_util_tests`.
- **SKLEARN_PROFILES clustering: exact on the profile-clustering bank**, now
  also through the server and CLI: they run `reference_profile_clustering_
  result` (TRACE_BASED log-to-features with the reference parameters,
  KMeans(n_clusters=2, random_state=0), max_iter 300, tol 1e-4). The flags are
  the reference parameters: `profile_include_activity` /
  `profile_include_succession` are `enable_activity_def_representation` /
  `enable_succ_def_representation` (default true), the trace/event
  string/numeric attribute lists are `str_tr_attr` / `str_ev_attr` /
  `num_tr_attr` / `num_ev_attr`, `profile_feature_names` is `feature_names`;
  verified against the reference in `minera_clustering_tests`. Other cluster
  counts and seeds (below 2^32) stand for that KMeans passed as
  `sklearn_clusterer` (declared). The native profile engine is a declared
  extension behind `profile_engine=native` /
  `--profile-clustering-engine native`.
- **Privacy (SaCoFa, PRIPEL) with secure randomness:** the OS-drawn seed is
  never emitted; diagnostics report seed 0 and no log line or response
  header carries it. The anonymization workbench keeps the same field set
  (12 SaCoFa/Laplace, 11 PRIPEL diagnostics fields) with `seed` 0 in secure
  mode; only `configured_options` echoes the seed the caller submitted, which
  the secure path ignores. SaCoFa diagnostics now report the candidate and selected
  violation counts.
- **Monte Carlo PETRI_SEMAPH_FIFO with `numpy_legacy_seed`:** exact on 426 of
  427 bank outcomes; see "Seeded Monte Carlo bank" for the residual.
- **Genetic miner:** invariant-only, see "Genetic discovery bank".

## Organizational metrics, POWL nets, defaults, statistics and XES nulls (2026-11-03)

Fixes:

- **Local diagnostics, group-attribute mode.** As the reference
  `apply_from_group_attribute`, a group is the set of resources seen with
  that `org:group` value, and every event of a member then counts for each of
  its groups, whatever group value (if any) that event carries: focus, stake
  and member contribution use these member events. Coverage alone stays on the
  tagged events (a member's share of the events tagged with the group). An
  event whose resource belongs to no group is skipped. Explicit-groups mode is
  unchanged. r1 doing A (g1), B (g2), A (untagged) and r2 doing A (g2) gives
  focus g1 {A: 2/3, B: 1}, stake g2 {A: 0.75, B: 0.25}, coverage g2 {r1: 0.5,
  r2: 0.5} and contribution g2 r1 {A: 2, B: 1}. Test:
  `minera_local_diagnostics_tests`.
- **`activity_completions` is one total per resource.** The reference
  `activity_completions(log, t1, t2, r)` takes no activity, so native returns
  one row per resource with an empty activity, counting every timestamped
  event of the resource in the slot; an activity selector no longer narrows
  it. Trace A, B, C by x gives 3. The organizational workspace hint and the
  frontend fixture follow. Test: `minera_resource_profiles_tests`.
- **`average_duration_activity`, `average_workload` and `multitasking` on
  lifecycle logs.** Imported CSV/XES logs follow the reference DataFrame path
  (the project policy above): every timestamped event takes part whatever its
  lifecycle, each case is stably sorted by timestamp, and an event's interval
  runs from the previous event of its case (the first from itself). B
  complete @0, D start @10, D complete @58 by x gives D 48 (the EventLog path
  pairs lifecycles). A start @0, B start @5, A complete @10, B complete @15 by
  alice gives workload 3.0 at t2 = 10 s (EventLog path 0.0). Fresh
  comparison against `read_xes` DataFrames: 3,200 random calls over all
  11 metrics, lifecycle logs included, differ only where the reference
  returns NaN or raises (declared below). Tests:
  `minera_resource_profiles_tests` (mixed, overlap, complete-start-complete
  and workload cases checked against the reference).
- **POWL to Petri net follows the reference construction.** No
  `reduce_petri_net` pass any more: the root sits between two inner places
  joined to source and sink by silent transitions; a choice puts its children
  between its own places; a loop enters its do part through a silent
  transition, runs its redo part from the do exit to its own place and back
  to the entry through a silent transition, and leaves through a silent exit;
  a partial order gets a silent split, one place per transitive-reduction
  edge, silent transitions after each child with successors and before each
  child with predecessors, and a silent join. Then the reference's simple
  reduction folds single-entry and then single-exit silent transitions. A
  `FrequentTransition` (optional or self-looping) is one visible transition
  labelled `"<label>\n[1,<max or ->]"`. Fresh comparison: 1,800/1,800 random
  POWL models (seeds 1 to 6, with and without frequency leaves) give
  isomorphic nets (places, labels, arcs, markings), so token-based
  generalization and simplicity on `discover_powl` nets now match. Tests:
  `minera_powl_conversion_tests` and the conversion banks.
- **Temporal-profile conformance zeta.** Requests through the shared request
  parser (the server's temporal-conformance routes) default `temporal_zeta`
  to 1.0, the `pm4py.conformance_temporal_profile` wrapper
  default; the library `TemporalProfileOptions` keeps the algorithm default
  of 6, as does streaming temporal conformance (no wrapper). Test:
  `minera_request_params_tests`.
- **Genetic defaults.** Server and CLI requests use the
  `pm4py.discover_petri_net_genetic` wrapper defaults (population 500,
  100 generations, elitism 0.01, crossover 1.0, mutation 0.01, tournament
  sample 5) with a candidate bound of 50,500 so the whole default search can
  run; a default tournament sample shrinks below a smaller explicit
  population. On `data/sample_event_log.csv` (13 activities) the default
  search took 28.2 s on a loaded 4-core machine (load average about 10) and
  stopped after 59 generations on its stable-fitness rule. The library
  `GeneticMinerOptions` keeps its native defaults (32/20/0.10/0.80/0.10/3,
  bound 10,000). Tests: `minera_request_params_tests`, frontend
  `discovery-model.test.ts`.
- **Attribute statistics use Python dict-key equality** (the FS5 rule):
  1, 1.0 and True are one key (0, 0.0 and False too), the string '1' stays
  apart, and each key keeps its first-seen cell, in both count modes and for
  trace attributes. The result gains `entries` (value, type, count in the
  reference dict's order, see the fresh sweep below); `values` stays the map
  by first-seen text, where keys that only share a text (the int 1 and the
  string '1') add up. Reference `{1: 6, 0: 2, '1': 1, 2.5: 1}` is native
  `entries` 1/int 6, 0/int 2, 1/str 1, 2.5/float 1. Test:
  `minera_attribute_statistics_tests`.
- **ALL_PREFIXES** prefix traces carry no trace attributes, properties or case
  id (see Log utilities above). Test: `minera_log_util_tests`.
- **Server XES downloads are pm4py-readable.** The default `read_xes` fails on
  a `null="true"` int, float or date and misreads the other kinds (boolean
  False, strings None; `line_by_line`/`chunk_regex` read the text "true"), so
  server XES (filtered log-query, cluster and clustering exports, preparation,
  anonymization, transformation and case-relation open logs, stream-reader and
  source-acquisition exports) now omits null attributes, as pm4py's writer
  does for None/NaN. `preserve_nulls=true` (or `xes_preserve_nulls=true` on
  the plain XES export) opts into the markers on the routes that take it; the
  frontend download helpers send `preserve_nulls=false` unless asked. Native
  CLI tools that write XES files keep their markers. Tests: frontend
  `source-acquisition-workspace.test.ts`, `reader-stream-workspace.test.ts`.

Declarations (the reference raises; native keeps its result):

- **Interval tree ties.** `log_to_intervals`, the open-paths interval tree
  and `convert_log_to_time_intervals` raise `TypeError: '<' not supported
  between instances of 'Event' and 'Event'` when two intervals tie on
  (start, end) with different source events (one trace A, B, C at one
  timestamp); native returns the intervals (2 there). 46 of 500 random logs;
  the other 454 match.
- **Resource-profile workload, multitasking and duration on lifecycle
  logs.** The reference EventLog path raises `IndexError` when a trace holds
  only unmatched start events and `ValueError('Start must be less than end')`
  when a derived interval is reversed (B start @10, B complete @20,
  A complete @15 by r3); native returns its value (0 or 1). The DataFrame
  `average_duration_activity` returns NaN when no event matches, where native
  raises "mean requires at least one data point" (a row cannot hold NaN), and
  raises `AttributeError: Can only use .dt accessor` on some empty
  selections, where native returns 0.
- **Local diagnostics, explicit groups.** The reference raises `KeyError`
  when a listed resource does not occur in the log; native computes with the
  resources that occur.
- **Frontend captures.** All 16 `*-request-manifest.json` sets were
  replayed with `scripts/capture-workbench-fixtures.py` against a server
  built from the 2026-11-04 working tree (a fresh server per manifest) and
  the changed entries recaptured with `--write` (1,008 of 2,673 entries;
  a second replay then matches every entry). The changes come from the
  intended work since the captures were taken: case order by case id,
  tree-to-net and reduction names, BPMN layout, token-replay precision,
  summary active-source snapshots, zeta 1 and POWL nets, the XES writer's
  NUL / invalid UTF-8 refusals, seeded playout and Monte Carlo draws,
  reference ports of the decomposed and tree alignments, and 7 entries that
  now answer 400 (normalized Levenshtein with an empty trace, strict XML,
  DFG playout seed range, tree playout bound). One change was a regression
  and was fixed instead (Monte Carlo arc weights, below). The script now
  keeps a manifest's CRLF line ends, refreshes the exports the input
  workbenches return as top-level fields (`pnml`, `ptml`, `bpmn`,
  `source_xes`, `model_export`, ...) and the embedding workbench's hex
  artifacts, which it used to drop; an export that is now null (the XES
  writer's refusals, the 400s) loses its record, as the tests expect, and
  one that is newly produced gets a record (2 entries). It also updates the
  expected status and the manifest fields that mirror the response
  (`operation`, `executed`, `error`, `native_calls`, `variant`, ...), which
  the fixture tests compare. The active-source fixture test accepts the
  summary snapshot that mining responses embed (complete states come from
  /api/active-source). The 48 frontend test files that read these
  fixtures pass.
  The recaptured entries are self-referential: `--write` takes their
  expected status and fields from Minera's own responses, so a clean replay
  shows that the fixtures match the current server, not that the server
  matches the reference. They are regression baselines, not parity
  evidence; in particular the 7 entries that now answer 400 and the changed
  conformance key order were not compared with the reference here.
  The standalone captures (not in a manifest) record only their source
  file's name, and none of those sources is in the repository, so they
  were not replayed and still hold their earlier output; their tests check
  internal consistency only. By source:
  - `owned-structured.csv` (11): `structured-discovery-inductive-*`

  - `owned-behavior.csv` (38): every `behavior-analysis-*` capture

  - `owned-adapters.csv` (2): `structured-discovery-{inductive,powl}-adapted`.
  - `owned-constraints.csv` (13): `constraint-discovery-{declare,skeleton}-*`.

  - `owned-discovery.csv` (7): `workflow-discovery-{alpha,heuristic}-*`.

## Process-tree DP one-child operators, CSV row shapes and Monte Carlo arc weights (2026-11-04)

- **DP process-tree alignment, one-child operators.** The
  `DYNAMIC_PROGRAMMING` port dereferenced a missing child when a sequence,
  parallel or loop operator had one child (a one-child loop crashed the
  server: `/api/align-process-tree-workbench` entry
  `dynamic_programming-native-one-body-loop`). The reference reads the
  second child (a loop's redo) by position and raises `IndexError` when it
  evaluates it; the port now raises at the same points and the dispatcher
  falls back to the native search ("native search (reference: list index out
  of range)"). A loop whose body fits the whole segment returns that body
  without reading the redo, as the reference does, so `*(a)` on `[a]` is the
  reference result (cost 0, fitness 1) and `[a, a]` falls back; an operator
  without children is refused before the DP runs. Fuzz: 8,400 random
  requests to `/api/align-process-tree-workbench` and
  `/api/align-graph-workbench` on an ASan build answer 200 or 400 only.
  Tests: `minera_process_tree_alignment_tests` (`one_child_operators`).
- **CSV row shapes follow `pandas.read_csv`.** The batch CSV importer now
  reads row lengths the way the default C parser does. When the first data
  row has k more fields than the header, its first k fields become the
  implicit index, which `format_dataframe` discards (a trailing delimiter on
  every row is the common case); a later row longer than header + k is
  refused with read_csv's own message, "Expected N fields in line L, saw M"
  (L counts records from the top of the file, blank lines included, a
  multi-line quoted record once), in a 400 that also says how many fields
  the rows may have; a short row is padded with empty (NaN) cells, so a row
  without its activity or case id is dropped, and so is one without a
  timestamp once the timestamp column holds dates (decided from every row),
  as `format_dataframe` drops it (see "CSV rows without a timestamp are
  dropped" below). Before,
  extra fields were ignored and short rows refused. The
  /api/mine size estimate already counted these rows and its columns are the
  header's, so its 413 decision is unchanged. Stream readers (csv.DictReader
  in the reference) keep their rules. Black-box fuzz against read_csv +
  format_dataframe, 3,000 files with random row lengths, blank and
  delimiter-only lines: every refusal matches pandas with the same N, L and
  M (802 files); every file both read gives the same rows apart from the
  timestamp and dtype policies of that run (rows without a timestamp were
  then kept and are now dropped, see below; unparseable or all-empty
  timestamp columns, which format_dataframe refuses, in 102 files). Tests:
  `minera_core_tests` (`follows_reference_csv_row_shapes`),
  `minera_server_parameter_contract_tests`.
- **Monte Carlo firing honours arc weights.** Since PNML parallel arcs are
  read as one weighted occurrence, Monte Carlo moved one token per arc and
  deadlocked nets with weighted or parallel arcs (a capture's net with two
  parallel inputs and a weight-2 output ended with 0 of 2 cases complete).
  Firing now moves each arc's weight, as the reference
  `semantics.execute` does (2 of 2 complete). Tests:
  `minera_monte_carlo_tests` (`weighted_and_parallel_arcs_move_their_weight`).

## Empty POWL orders, POWL frequency bounds, alignment stop reasons, disconnect cancellation and untimed CSV rows (2026-11-04)

- **Empty POWL partial orders.** `convert_to_petri_net` gives an empty
  partial order (`PO=(nodes={}, order={})`) a silent split with no outputs
  and a silent join with no inputs, wherever it is nested; native built one
  silent `in -> out` step (2 places and 1 transition at the top level where
  the reference has 2 and 2). The general partial-order construction now
  runs for no children too, and the simple reduction repeats its
  single-entry and single-exit passes until neither folds, because a
  single-exit fold next to an empty order can open a single-entry fold
  (`PO=(nodes={A, PO=(nodes={}, order={})}, order={})` is one `A` from
  source to sink in both). Fresh comparison through
  `/api/model-conversion-workbench`: 4,800 random POWL models (where
  counted, 233 of 4,200 hold an empty order and 1,478 a new frequency
  bound) give isomorphic nets in 4,799; the earlier 1,800-model bank still
  matches 1,800/1,800. Declared:
  the reference compares partial orders by value, so two empty orders that
  are children of one partial order are one node of its order relation; it
  then keeps an extra silent transition without arcs, or raises
  `ValueError: Cannot generate transitive reduction! Reflexivity detected!`
  when one precedes the other. Native treats them as distinct children (the
  one remaining diff above). Tests: `minera_powl_conversion_tests`
  (`empty_partial_order_matches_reference_nets`).
- **POWL frequency bounds.** The text form `T("label",min,max|*)` now takes
  any nonnegative bounds, as `FrequentTransition(label, min, max)` does: a
  minimum of 0 is skippable, an unbounded maximum (`*`, the reference's
  `"-"`) self-loops, and other values only change the label
  (`T("A",0,3)` is `"A\n[1,3]"`, `T("A",2,*)` is `"A\n[1,-]"`, `T("A",2,5)`
  is `"A"`). Native refused anything but 0/1 and 1/unbounded. `self_loop()`
  is now exactly "unbounded maximum" (a finite maximum above 1 used to
  count), and the process-tree conversion maps the two flags as before
  (optional: `X(tau, a)`, self-loop: `*(a, tau)`). Negative bounds have no
  text form and are still refused by the native constructor. Tests:
  `minera_powl_tests`, `minera_powl_conversion_tests`
  (`frequency_bounds_follow_reference_flags`).
- **Why an alignment search stopped.** An exhausted `/api/align` result
  (and every serializer that writes `AlignmentResult`) now carries
  `time_limit_reached`: true when a configured time limit (`max_align_time`
  or `max_align_time_trace`) had run out, false when the state limit stopped
  the search with time to spare. Computed and unsound results do not carry
  the key. The Conformance view gives the app's 60-second time-budget advice
  only when a time limit stopped the search, names the state limit when that
  stopped it, and no longer says partial numbers are hidden (no fitness,
  precision or cost exists for such a run). A time-stopped result (or one
  from a server that does not say) is not cached, so reopening the view
  retries; state-bound results stay cached, as they are deterministic.
  Native extension (the reference has no time limit). Tests:
  `minera_alignment_variants_tests`, `alignment-uncomputed.test.ts`.
- **Disconnect cancellation.** `/api/genetic-mine` (and
  `/api/genetic-matrix-convert`), `/api/ilp-mine` and `/api/evaluate`
  (alignment-based fitness and precision) now stop when the client
  disconnects, as `/api/align` already did, through the same
  `Request::is_connection_closed` hook: the genetic miner polls before each
  candidate's fitness replay, ILP before each pair LP, every 16 simplex
  pivots and before each implicit-place LP, and alignment-based precision
  before each prefix (its alignments use `AlignmentOptions::cancelled`). A
  cancelled run throws `OperationCancelled` and returns nothing, so no
  partial result is cached. Measured on the sample log (genetic) and a
  noisy 14-activity log (ILP, alignment-based fitness), closing the socket
  1 s after sending: in the 9 s from sending, the previous server used
  8.9 s of CPU for each (it kept computing), the new one 1.0 to 1.3 s (the
  second before the close). Uncancelled responses match the previous
  server (timing fields aside) on 21 of 23 genetic, ILP, evaluate and align
  requests; the other two differ only by the new `time_limit_reached` key
  and a time-limited search's counters. Native extension. Tests: `minera_genetic_miner_tests`,
  `minera_ilp_miner_tests`.
- **CSV rows without a timestamp are dropped.** `format_dataframe` drops a
  row whose timestamp is NA (an empty cell or a pandas NA spelling) together
  with rows missing a case id or activity, with its "Some rows of the Pandas
  data frame have been removed" warning; a case left without rows
  disappears. The batch CSV importer kept those rows as untimed events. It
  now drops them once the timestamp column converts to dates. The column is
  converted before any row is dropped, so the decision reads every row,
  including rows without a case id or activity: a date on such a row still
  makes the column dates (and the untimed kept rows go), and a cell there
  that cannot be converted refuses the frame like one on a kept row. A
  literal `NaT`, `NAT` or `nat` is a missing date (its row is dropped, and a
  column of them alone converts and loses every row); other spellings such
  as `Nat` refuse. A whitespace-only timestamp is text to `to_datetime`, so
  with dates in the column it refuses the frame although `trim_fields`
  blanks other whitespace ("CSV row N has a whitespace-only timestamp").
  A column with no date keeps every row, as before (the reference refuses
  such a frame: "the dataframe should (at least) contain a column of type
  date"), and stream readers keep NA spellings as literal values. The CSV
  row-shape entry above states the same policy. Declared, not matched: with
  an implicit index the reference's columns shift, and `format_dataframe`
  then also converts date-like text in a shifted case-id or activity column
  (activity `2024-01-01T00:37:00` becomes `2024-01-01 00:37:00+00:00`), and
  it drops NaN-timestamp rows when any other column holds dates although the
  timestamp column holds none; native converts the selected timestamp column
  only. A timestamp padded with spaces is trimmed (`" NaT"` is then
  dropped, where the reference refuses it; padded dates parse on both
  sides). Fresh comparison against `read_csv` + `format_dataframe` +
  `convert_to_event_log` on 2,000 random files (NaT spellings,
  whitespace-only cells and dates only on dropped rows included): all 516
  read refusals match; of the 917 files the reference reads, 862 give the
  same cases and activity sequences and the other 55 are the implicit-index
  shifts above (53 differ, 2 refused by native); of the 567 the reference
  refuses, native refuses 238 and keeps the 329 whose column has no date.
  The tree before this change matched 796 of the 917 and kept 93 refused
  frames with date-like text in the column (whitespace or NaT cells next to
  dates, mostly). Tests: `minera_core_tests`
  (`csv_import_matches_reference_dataframe_flow`,
  `follows_reference_csv_row_shapes`),
  `minera_server_parameter_contract_tests`.

## Arc weights and parallel arcs across Petri code paths (2026-11-04)

Since PNML import keeps parallel arcs and zero, signed or large weights as
one weighted occurrence per arc object (a weight-w arc otherwise becomes w
repeated endpoints), every path that moved or checked one token per endpoint
was audited. Black-box comparisons used random nets with weights 1 to 3 and
parallel duplicates (49 + 55 general nets with random markings; 39 + 60
workflow nets from random process trees with scaled, unbalanced and parallel
arcs), written by the reference `write_pnml` and read by both sides; the
second set of each was fresh after the fixes.

Changed to follow the reference:
- **Marking equation and Woflan invariants.** The classic marking equation
  adds -1/+1 per arc object, whatever its weight (parallel arcs count twice),
  as `incidence_matrix.construct` does, so DC4 is lifted. Woflan's
  S-component, uniform and weighted invariant stages use a weighted incidence
  (each arc object adds its signed weight: weights 2 and -1 in parallel sum to
  1), which reproduces the reference's uncovered places on every probe. On a
  net with weighted or parallel arcs that is not S-coverable both soundness
  variants now report unsound, as `check_soundness` and `woflan` do on every
  such net probed (even when the net behaves soundly); an S-coverable one
  keeps the behavioural verdict. Reachability, coverability and the
  restricted coverability tree fire each arc by its weight. Fresh workflow
  nets: soundness 60/60; Woflan 38/38 where the reference returns (it raises
  `AttributeError: module 'pm4py.util.nx_utils' has no attribute
  'topological_sort'` on the other 22, after printing "unsound"; native
  answers unsound).
- **Alignment dispatcher on weighted or parallel arcs.** The easy-soundness
  gate follows the reference check as observed: the LP relaxation of the
  arc-object marking equation must be feasible, and the final marking must
  be reachable when a transition needs the summed weight of its arcs from a
  place, takes one arc's weight there and puts the summed weight of its
  output arcs; a search beyond `max_states` refuses the net (1,483 of 1,500
  random nets with parallel arcs agree; the rest are unbounded or tie
  cases). As a native extension, the trace options' `max_time_seconds`
  refuses it the same way and `cancelled` stops it with OperationCancelled,
  as they bound the alignment searches themselves. The searches that run on the synchronous product (state-equation
  A*, Dijkstra without heuristics, discounted A*) see every arc object with
  weight 1 and, like the reference, enable a transition with k parallel arcs
  from a place at k tokens there but take one (`<a, c, b>` costs 20001 where
  firing the net would give 0); DIJKSTRA_LESS_MEMORY fires the net itself
  with its weights, as its reference variant does. Fresh workflow nets 60/60,
  fresh general nets 52/55 (two the reference refuses, one negative-token
  net).
- **BPMN conversion** draws one flow per arc object (a weight-2 arc once, two
  parallel arcs twice), as `convert_to_bpmn` does.
- **Decision mining, decision tables and data Petri nets** count a place's
  out-arc objects: one weight-2 arc is no decision point, while two parallel
  arcs to one transition are one (the reference lists `{'p1': ['b', 'b']}`);
  a firing gives one row per decision place.
- **Stochastic Petri reachability, the stochastic map and model decorations**
  move each arc's weight (decorations keep tokens as runs of equal instants).
  A decoration keeps a place's first 2^24 wait samples one by one and any
  further ones as runs of one value, so a huge weight never fails a mine:
  such a place's count saturates at 2^64 - 1 and its total adds value ×
  count per run (native extension; places within the bound are summarized
  exactly as before).
  The older Petri usage comparison replay moves one token per endpoint, so a
  weighted or parallel-arc net goes through the token-replay composition.
- **Footprints of a net** build their reachability graph with the shared
  weighted firing.
- **Frontend Petri renderer** draws one arc per arc object and labels weights
  other than 1.

Already weight-aware, rechecked: token replay (R1; fresh 54/55, one
set-order tie), streaming token replay (S5), basic and extensive playout
(fresh 55/55 and 60/60), Monte Carlo (entry above), net footprints (55/55,
60/60), PNML export (each arc with its weight, 55/55). Not applicable: OCPN
(discovered nets have unit arcs; variable arcs are flags) and PTML (trees).

Kept as native behaviour, declared:
- **Negative tokens.** `semantics.execute` subtracts every arc and can leave a
  negative count (two parallel unit arcs from a one-token place give -1);
  native consumption stops at zero, as `weak_execute` does. Nets that reach
  such markings differ in reachability, marking equation and alignments.
- **Fractional marking equations.** The reference solves the LP and returns
  `int()` of the objective and of each count (1.5 gives 1); native solves the
  integer program (`lower_bound` keeps the LP optimum), so a fractional
  optimum differs (6 of the 115 fresh nets).
- **Decomposed alignments** are unchanged: the reference port reads a weight-w
  arc as w unit arcs, which keeps the pinned agreement on the conformance
  bank (routing weighted nets to the native search lost three rows), and a
  compact side uses the native search. Not compared further: the reference
  decomposition does not return on a direct weight-2 probe.
- **Reduction** returns a net with a compact side unchanged (its rules rewrite
  unit endpoints only).
- Interactive conformance on compact sides stays gated; its message now names
  parallel arcs.

Found, not arc related: `convert_to_bpmn` connects the end event from
every place of the final marking; native connected the sink only, so all 12
fresh general nets whose final marking holds two or more places differed by
one flow (and two by one node). Fixed in the next section.

Tests: `minera_petri_analysis_tests` (`weighted_marking_equation_counts_arc_objects`,
`woflan_weighted_and_parallel_arcs`, `alignment_weighted_and_parallel_arcs`,
`classic_equation_requires_integer_solutions`), `minera_decision_table_tests`
(`weighted_arc_is_not_a_decision_point`), `minera_stochastic_petri_tests`
(`weighted_arcs_move_their_weight`), `minera_petri_net_reduction_tests`
(`compact_arc_nets_are_kept`), `minera_core_tests`
(`decorate_model_moves_arc_weights`), frontend `petri-layout.test.ts`.

## BPMN marking events, OCEL CSV row shapes and disconnect cancellation coverage (2026-11-04)

- **BPMN from a marked net.** `convert_to_bpmn(net, im, fm)` always creates
  the start and end events, draws a flow from the start event to every place
  with tokens in the initial marking and from every place with tokens in the
  final marking to the end event (empty markings leave the events
  unconnected; a place in both markings with no arcs becomes start → end once
  its one-in, one-out gateway collapses). Native drew them from the source
  and sink only. `to_bpmn(net, initial_marking, final_marking)` (and
  `write_bpmn`) now follow the markings; `to_bpmn(net)` keeps the
  source/sink form, which equals the marked form for a workflow net with one
  token on each. Fresh comparison through the PNML reader with the markings
  as written: 80 random general nets (41 with two or more initially marked
  places, 48 with two or more finally marked places, 11 and 7 with an empty
  marking, 78 with weighted arcs) and 60 workflow nets from random trees
  (56 with weights, 51 with parallel arc elements) match nodes, task names,
  gateway directions and the flow multiset in 140 of 140 (12 of 55 general
  nets differed before). The server's model-exchange route still refuses
  BPMN for nets that are not single-token workflow nets, unchanged. Tests:
  `minera_bpmn_reference_parity_tests` (six new general-net cases: several
  marked places, empty markings, a place in both markings, a pass-through
  weighted place, an inner final place, a random weighted net).
- **OCEL CSV row shapes.** `pm4py.read_ocel_csv` reads both tables with
  `pandas.read_csv`, and the native reader now follows it: blank lines
  (empty or spaces and tabs only) are skipped but still counted; the first
  data row sets the width (the header's or longer: the extra fields are
  dropped, as pandas does with a ParserWarning); a later, longer row refuses
  the file with the pandas message (`Expected N fields in line L, saw M`,
  where L counts records, header and blank lines included, and a multi-line
  quoted field once); short rows read missing cells. Quoting follows the C
  tokenizer: a quote opens a quoted field only as its first character, text
  after a closing quote is appended (`"A"x` reads `Ax`), `""` is a quote
  inside quotes, quoted fields may span lines, and an unterminated quote
  refuses the file. An event row with a missing id or activity is dropped
  (and, without an object table, its objects are still listed, as the
  reference collects them from every row); an object row with a missing id
  or type is dropped. The reference parses the timestamp column before it
  drops rows, so a dropped row with an unreadable timestamp still refuses
  the file. Fresh fuzz (400 random event tables, 172 with an object table,
  short, long and very short rows, blank lines, quoting): 145 both refuse
  with the same pandas message, 4 both refuse a bad timestamp, 176 read the
  same events, relations and objects, and 75 the same except as declared
  below (before the duplicate fix below: 123, 48 and 80 refused natively).
  Declared: an event with a
  missing timestamp is NaT in the reference and refused natively (`event
  CSV event X has no timestamp`), since a native event needs an instant;
  fields stay trimmed by default, also object reference cells, so
  `" ['o1']"` relates `o1` natively where pandas keeps the leading space
  and the reference lists no objects for that cell (`trim_fields=false`
  matches the reference; declared); NA spellings (`NA`, `null`, ...) in
  attribute cells stay text where pandas reads NaN; a header-only file reads
  as an empty log where pm4py raises KeyError; an object an event names but
  the object table lacks is added natively (type from its column, no
  attributes) so its relations resolve, where the reference keeps the
  relation and lists no object (the 75). Fixed: an object listed twice in
  one cell (`"['o1', 'o1']"`) was refused (`duplicate object id in one event
  row`), and the CSV writer refused repeated relations. The reference keeps
  one relation per list entry, and the native reader and writer now do the
  same. Downstream, the reference counts the repeats in the statistics
  (`objects_ot_count`, activity and object-type associations), draws
  self-loops in the OC-DFG, repeats the event in the flattened trace, writes
  them to OCEL 2.0 JSON, XML and SQLite and to CSV, and reads them back from
  XML, SQLite and CSV, while the OCEL 2.0 JSON and classic readers dedupe.
  Native output matches each of these on a fixture with repeats in two
  object types (0 OC-DFG differences; the same relations in every export;
  the same read-back in both directions). Declared, unchanged: the native
  `edge_associations` statistic counts an event-object pair once, so it
  lacks the self-loop associations of `find_associations_per_edge` (this
  applies to repeats from XML and SQLite input too). On the server,
  `POST /api/ocel/io` CSV imports return the repeats in both JSON documents,
  but the OCEL analysis and export routes take OCEL JSON, whose readers
  dedupe as `read_ocel_json` and `read_ocel2_json` do, so the server
  computes as the reference does after a JSON round trip; the CLI keeps the
  repeats from a CSV, XML or SQLite input. Tests:
  `minera_ocel_csv_tests` (`follows_reference_csv_row_shapes`,
  `keeps_repeated_relations`).
- **OCEL CSV object cells, lone carriage returns and written timestamps.**
  Object cells now read as `pm4py.read_ocel_csv` reads them (observed
  black-box): a cell that does not start with `[` or is no Python literal
  (`[o1]`, `['o1'`, `[1+1]`, `[float('nan')]`, `['o1']x`) lists no objects
  and its event stays, on kept and dropped rows alike (natively `[o1]` read
  as `o1` and a malformed list refused the file). Elements become ids as
  pandas prints them in one column typed from every element of every cell:
  `str()` of each when any element is text (`[1, 'a', True, 1e3, 3j, b'x']`
  lists `1`, `a`, `True`, `1000.0`, `3j`, `x`), floats or complex numbers
  when the elements are numbers and None alone (`[1]` next to `[None]`
  relates `1.0`); None and empty strings are skipped; string prefixes,
  escapes, implicit concatenation, comments and newlines follow Python.
  Without an object table a list, set or dict element raises the
  reference's TypeError (`unhashable type`), and bytes that are not UTF-8
  its UnicodeDecodeError; both refuse natively. In the event-log CSV and
  OCEL CSV readers, a delimiter right after a skipped blank line that a
  lone `\r` ends is dropped, as pandas' tokenizer drops it (`\r\r,5,6`
  reads 5,6; also before the header). The OCEL CSV writer prints the
  timestamp column as `DataFrame.to_csv` does: a naive column of midnights
  as dates (`2024-01-01`, the year unpadded), other naive columns with the
  fraction digits their most precise value needs on every value (3, 6 or
  9), and an aware column value by value in the offset its values share.
  Fuzz: 400 random OCEL event tables (object cells of every kind above,
  `\n`, `\r\n` and lone `\r` endings, blank lines, rows starting with the
  delimiter, about 30% with an object table): 192 read the same events, relations
  and objects, 74 the same except the declared added objects, 69 both
  refuse, 36 refused as declared below, 28 refused for an id under two
  types (unchanged), 1 differs (a header starting with the delimiter, which
  pandas names `Unnamed: 0`; unchanged); 400 random event-log CSVs with the
  same line endings through `/api/mine`: 318 the same rows, 66 both refuse,
  16 differ, all with that unnamed header column (unchanged). Declared: a
  line starting with spaces or tabs after a blank line a lone `\r` ends,
  which pandas misreads (it returns 131,073 rows of NaN for one such line),
  is refused; tuple elements (and, with an object table, the list, set and
  dict elements the reference prints) and well-formed `\N{NAME}` escapes
  in a cell that otherwise parses are refused, since this reader has no
  Unicode name table (the reference relates `'\N{BULLET}'` as `•` and
  lists nothing for an unknown name); a malformed `\N` escape (`'\N'`,
  `'\N{}'`, `'\N{BULLET'`, `'\N{A_B}'`) or one in a cell that is no
  literal (`['\N{BULLET}', o3]`) lists no objects, as in the reference,
  and raw strings and bytes keep it as text (observed black-box on
  `pm4py.read_ocel_csv`);
  values whose relation ids and object ids disagree in the reference
  (`[1, 1.0]`, `[1, '1']`, `[True]` next to `[1]`, or `[1]` next to `[None]`
  without an object table, where the reference lists object `1.0` for
  relations `1`, or the reverse) are refused, as a native OCEL cannot hold
  relations to missing or repeated object ids. Unchanged: OCEL JSON and XML
  readers keep a naive timestamp naive where the reference stores it as
  UTC, so a CSV written from such a log prints it naive (now as a date at
  midnight) where the reference prints `+00:00`. Tests:
  `minera_ocel_csv_tests` (`reads_object_cells_as_pandas`,
  `writes_timestamps_as_pandas`), `minera_core_tests`
  (`csv_import_matches_reference_dataframe_flow`).
- **Disconnect cancellation coverage.** The connection hook now also stops
  process-tree alignment (the four reference ports per trace, the native
  search per trace and every 256 expansions), decomposed alignment (per
  variant in the reference port, per trace and search step natively), DFG
  alignment (per search step and per variant), edit-distance alignment (per
  target comparison), token replay forward and backward (per trace; also the
  token conformance check, its precision prefix walk and Monte Carlo's
  fitting replay), concept drift (per sub-log and permutation), Monte Carlo
  (per scheduler event), the Petri, process-tree and graph alignment
  workbenches, the replay workbenches, `/api/evaluate`'s decomposed fitness
  and `/api/mine`: between its stages, inside the reachability search, the
  conformance check and the model decorations, which take most of a mine
  (about 120 of 140 s on the log below). A cancelled call throws
  `OperationCancelled`; every route answers 400 and a cancelled mine
  publishes nothing. Measured on a 5,000-case, 50,000-event log over 14
  random activities, closing the socket during the run: edit distance
  against itself (35 s uncancelled) closed at 3 s used 7.8 s of CPU in the
  next 8 s on the previous server and 0.06 s on the new one; `/api/mine`
  closed at 30 s 7.9 s and 0.10 s; closing a mine at 4, 6, 8, 10, 13, 16 or
  20 s stops it within 0.15 s of CPU. Uncancelled responses are byte-equal
  to the previous server for process-tree, DFG, decomposed and edit-distance
  alignment and concept drift, and the mine response differs only in its
  `source_id` counter. Concept drift's work bounds cap a run at about a
  second, so it is never long. The session discovery routes measured
  (`/api/discover-workflow` alpha, heuristic, IMf and POWL) answer in under
  a second on this log and are not hooked. Native extension. Tests:
  `minera_cancellation_hooks_tests` (each hook polls, leaves an uncancelled
  result unchanged and throws once it fires; DFG alignment, concept drift,
  Monte Carlo and edit distance stop within a second of a disconnect),
  `minera_server_cancellation_tests` (edit distance and two mines stop
  within a second of the client closing; the server keeps serving).

## CSV header names, OCEL ids under two types and naive OCEL timestamps (2026-11-04)

Three gaps left open by the previous round (its "Unchanged" items on the
unnamed CSV header column, the OCEL id under two types and naive OCEL JSON/XML
timestamps) are closed or declared. All evidence is black-box PM4Py 2.7.22
(pandas 3.0.5) calls.

- **CSV header names follow `pandas.read_csv`.** The event-log CSV importer
  (batch path) and the OCEL CSV reader name columns as pandas does: an empty
  name becomes `Unnamed: <position>` (a header starting or ending with the
  delimiter, `a,,b`, and a blank name left by trimming), duplicates become
  `a.1`, `a.2`, ... (named columns first, then the unnamed ones, skipping
