## Review BR1: re-review of round BQ, CSV headers on the model routes, the log families on nanosecond CSV cells, DFG precision on CSV uploads, and the CLI's CSV modes (2026-11-12)

Round BR checked BQ's CI run (43314774208: all six jobs green, the Windows
ctest included; BP's run 43304285286 is green on all six jobs too),
re-reviewed BQ (the spectrum components' `order_key` and `log_instant`, the
temporal profile's `python_epoch` callers, the correlation miner's
`python_epoch_seconds`, `inductive_log_for_key`) and took BQ's targets: the
routes on the cached model logs keyed by a CSV's own header, the remaining
log families on nanosecond cells, DFG precision and alpha keyed by a
timestamp or lifecycle header, the Petri comparison with a CSV reference
log, and the CLI's other CSV modes. The device check on the Mac was skipped
(no device linked). Findings, all fixed:

- **BR1-1 The model routes keyed by a CSV's own header.** pm4py's frame of a
  CSV upload holds the selected column under its header (`act`) and under
  `concept:name`, so both keys give one answer. Minera's cached model logs
  hold one spelling: the Inductive log projects the miner's key over the
  header, the alpha and heuristics logs keep the header. On 20 uploads (50
  route and miner pairs each), the header failed 259 times on the Inductive
  model (alignments, the process-tree alignment, evaluation, decomposed,
  anti- and multi-alignments, decisions, decision tables, the data Petri
  net, Monte Carlo: `event is missing activity attribute 'act'`) and
  `concept:name` failed 122 times on the alpha and heuristics models
  (evaluation, Monte Carlo). A key that names the selected column under
  either spelling now reads the model's own log (`csv_activity_alias`,
  `model_key_field`), on every route that takes an explicit key on a cached
  model.
- **BR1-2 The Petri comparison with a CSV reference log.**
  `/api/compare-petri` read a CSV reference under the standard headers only
  (`CSV column not found: case:concept:name` on every upload with its own
  headers, all three miners). A CSV reference is now read with the
  session's selectors first, and the standard headers stay the fallback;
  the alpha model's default key is its own log's.
- **BR1-3 The batches on nanosecond cells.** pm4py's log variant reads
  `Timestamp.timestamp()` (rounded to the microsecond) and the pandas
  variant a `datetime64[ns]` column's int64 nanoseconds over 1e9 (one
  rounding of the integer to a double first: `1577836800.0000005` for
  600 ns past the second). Minera read the exact seconds in both: 20 of 30
  log answers and 3 of 30 pandas answers differed on the server, 22 and 5
  in the CLI (`log_instant`, `pandas_nanoseconds`).
- **BR1-4 The trace-based and temporal features on nanosecond cells.** The
  trace-based time features (case duration, times from the first and last
  occurrence, path times) read `Timestamp.timestamp()` floats
  (`python_epoch`). The temporal features read a CSV column with nanosecond
  cells as nanosecond instants (`csv_nanosecond_column`; the frame's cells
  are `datetime64[ns]` then) and divide the nanoseconds exactly before the
  six-digit rounding, as `Timestamp.timestamp()` does (600 ns past a second
  is 0.000001; the double of the int64 gave 0). Before, 22 of 30 trace-based
  answers and 19 of 30 temporal answers grouped by the second differed (27
  and 19 grouped by the minute with a start column).
- **BR1-5 The interval tree on nanosecond cells.** pm4py's
  `log_to_interval_tree` reads `Timestamp.timestamp()` floats; Minera read
  the exact seconds (27 of 30 trees differed).
- **BR1-6 The stochastic map's durations.** pm4py's replay map takes
  `Timedelta.total_seconds()` of the exact instants, which drops the
  nanoseconds of the difference (`7.999999999 - 1.0000014` is `6.999998`).
  Minera subtracted the parsed seconds: 9 of 30 fitted maps differed
  (`elapsed_seconds` on exact token times).
- **BR1-7 DFG precision on a CSV upload.** `/api/dfg-precision` without an
  activity key (the frontend's default) or with `concept:name` gave every
  event an empty activity on a CSV upload, so the precision was 0 or the
  escaping-edge share of the start activities: the route converts the
  session log to a stream and back, and that log holds the column under its
  header only. The key is now mapped to the header (`csv_frame_key`), as
  pm4py reads `concept:name` on the frame: 28 of 30 answers differed with
  `concept:name` and 28 of 30 without a key, all equal now. Round BQ's check of this route (`hdrkeys.py`) sent the key as a
  multipart field, which the route does not read (the frontend sends it in
  the query string), so it compared the default with itself.

Checked without findings: the CLI's default analysis of a CSV input against
the server's mine route and on-demand alignments (100 inputs: plain,
blanks, nanosecond cells, standard headers; footprints, Declare, log
skeleton, conformance, temporal profile, transition system and the other
sections); the CLI's footprints, Declare and log skeleton discovery against
pm4py on the frame (200 inputs); DFG precision and alpha keyed by a
lifecycle column (`life` and `lifecycle:transition`); passed time and Monte
Carlo case arrival on nanosecond uploads; BQ's sweeps on fresh seeds.

Declarations:

- Alpha (and the other miners) keyed by a date column: pm4py's transition
  labels are `str()` of the frame's UTC `Timestamp`
  (`2020-01-01 00:00:00+00:00`, `...00:00.500000+00:00`); Minera keeps the
  cell's text. The nets are otherwise equal (60 of 60 uploads). DFG
  precision keyed by a date column has no reference answer: pm4py's
  `discover_dfg` refuses a date activity column and `write_dfg` a `Timestamp`
  key.
- `/api/stochastic-map` fails as a whole when the stochastic Petri net's
  reachability analysis (a Minera addition the route always runs) meets an
  immediate closure without a tangible resolution (5 of 30 Inductive models
  of nanosecond uploads); the fitted map, pm4py's part, equals pm4py's on
  the other 25.
- Number-keyed DataFrame routes, the CSV timestamp columns of plain numbers
  and "roles to diagnostics groups" (round AT) stay as declared.

Verification (scripts in the project files under `review-harness/round-br/`;
"before" is round BQ's CLI and server on the same scripts and seeds):

| Check | Comparisons | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Model routes keyed by `act` vs `concept:name` (`indkeys.py`: 20 uploads, 20 with blank activities; alignments, the process-tree alignment, evaluation with four adapters and three families, decomposed, anti- and multi-alignments, decisions, decision tables, data Petri net, Monte Carlo, Petri comparison with the CSV as reference, tree reduction; three miners) | 2,000 | before (the first 20): 259 refused the header, 122 refused `concept:name`, 60 Petri comparisons refused the CSV reference; after: 1,973 the same, 27 fail alike (search limits on the alpha and heuristics models, Monte Carlo cases without visible events) |
| Batches (log, pandas, Polars) on the server vs pm4py (`batchns.py`: 30 nanosecond uploads, 30 with a start column and blanks) | 180 | before (the first 30): 23 differed; after: all equal, 30 raise alike |
| CLI batches vs pm4py (`clibatchns.py`, 30 nanosecond inputs) | 90 | before: 27 differed; after: all equal |

## Review BS1: re-review of round BR, typed columns as activity keys, the stochastic map's reachability, the LLM abstractions on nanosecond cells and multipart fields on query-only routes (2026-11-13)

Round BS checked BR's CI run (43335386677: all six jobs green, the macOS and
Windows ctest included), re-reviewed BR (`csv_activity_alias`,
`model_key_field` and `supplies_model_field` on the model routes, the
compare-petri CSV reference, DFG precision's `csv_frame_key`, the batches,
features, interval tree and stochastic map on nanosecond cells) and took
BR's targets: date and other typed columns as activity keys across the
miners, the stochastic-map route's reachability failure, the remaining log
families on nanosecond cells, routes on XES uploads with nanosecond dates
and the multipart fields of query-only routes. The device check on the Mac
was skipped (no device linked). Findings, all fixed:

- **BS1-1 Typed columns as activity keys on the workflow miners.** pm4py's
  EventLog algorithms read the typed cells of a CSV upload's frame. Alpha
  and alpha plus label a transition `str()` of the cell (a date column's UTC
  `Timestamp`, `2021-03-01 00:00:00+00:00`; an integer `1`; the timestamp
  column; `@@index`); the heuristics miner raises TypeError at the first
  directly-follows pair holding a cell that is no `str` (`'Timestamp'
  object is not subscriptable` when the first element is one, `'<' not
  supported between instances of 'str' and 'T'` when the second is);
  Inductive raises on any key that is no `str` (`'<' not supported between
  instances of 'T' and 'str'` beside text, `__str__ returned non-string
  (type T)` for one distinct value, else `can only concatenate str (not
  "T") to str`); POWL labels `str()` unless text sits beside such a cell,
  where it raises the `'<'` TypeError. A missing cell is `NaT` in a date
  column and `nan` (a float) elsewhere. Minera kept the cell's CSV text and
  discovered on every key (BR declared the date labels); the heuristics
  miner keyed by another text column (the case column) also kept the
  activity column's labels. On 10 uploads, 11 keys and five miners, 274 of
  550 answers differed. The miners now project the key through
  `frame_keyed_activities` (`frame_keys.cpp`) and raise pm4py's errors
  (`frame_keyed_heuristics_error`, `frame_keyed_inductive_error`,
  `frame_keyed_powl_error`), on CSV and XES uploads.
- **BS1-2 POWL in the Petri comparison on a CSV upload's own headers.**
  `/api/compare-petri` with the POWL model projected both logs on the
  session's POWL key, `concept:name`, which the logs of a CSV upload with its
  own headers hold under the header: every such comparison raised
  `KeyError: 'concept:name'`. A key that names the upload's activity column
  now leaves the projection on the logs' own activity field, and an
  explicit key projects both logs as before.
- **BS1-3 The stochastic map's reachability.** `/api/stochastic-map` failed
  as a whole when the stochastic Petri reachability analysis, a Minera
  addition the route always runs, could not take the fitted map (BR
  declared 5 of 30 Inductive models of nanosecond uploads: a fitted normal
  with a negative mean, rows out of time order, has no CTMC rate). The
  fitted map, pm4py's part, is now returned with the reachability marked
  exhausted and a `CTMC unavailable: ...` diagnostic
  (`stochastic_map_reachability`, also the CLI's); a wrong-size initial
  marking still fails.
- **BS1-4 The LLM abstractions on nanosecond cells.** pm4py's
  `abstract_event_stream` prints a `datetime64[ns]` cell's `Timestamp` with
  nine fraction digits (`00:00:00.000000600`); the variants' and the DFG's
  durations read the exact nanoseconds; `abstract_log_attributes` takes a
  date column's quantiles through numpy's linear interpolation on the int64
  units (the neighbours' difference in int64, a float lerp: 600 ns past the
  second reads `.000000512`). Minera printed and measured microseconds and
  interpolated the exact instants: on 30 nanosecond uploads, 56 of 150
  answers differed (event stream 28, log attributes 27, variants 1). The
  abstractions now keep a cell's nanoseconds (`LogClock`,
  `numpy_int_quantile` in `llm_abstractions.cpp`).
- **BS1-5 Multipart fields on query-only routes.** Routes that take their
  controls in the query string read only their upload parts from a
  multipart body and dropped any other part silently (BR's finding: a
  check that sent DFG precision's key as a form field compared the default
  with itself). Such a part is now rejected with `multipart field NAME is
  not read by ROUTE; send controls in the query string`, as `/api/mine`
  rejects query parameters beside its upload, on 30 routes: DFG precision,
  import and conversion, model exchange, the process cube, the five
  streaming routes, the 14 OCEL routes, Petri reduction, both PRIPEL routes,
  the case-relation merge, timestamp interleavings and EMD. The frontend
  sends only the upload parts there. Routes that read their controls from
  either the query or the form (the replay, alignment and comparison
  uploads) are unchanged.

Checked without findings: the model routes keyed by a CSV's own header on
the POWL and imported models (alignments, evaluation with its adapters and
families, decomposed, anti- and multi-alignments, decisions, decision
tables, data Petri net, Monte Carlo, the Petri comparison); XES uploads
with sub-microsecond dates against the same dates truncated to the
microsecond (pm4py's `read_xes` truncates; the mine body, performance DFG,
case statistics, sojourn time, interval tree, stochastic map and passed
time agree); service time, cycle time and case arrival on nanosecond CSV
cells against pm4py's pandas functions; the stochastic map's fitted timing
(BR's sweep on fresh seeds).

Declarations:

- A blank cell of a float or text column as an activity key: pm4py's
  EventLog holds each float NaN as its own object, so alpha, alpha plus and
  POWL give every blank event a separate `nan` activity and the heuristics
  miner an isolated `nan` node; Minera labels them one `nan` activity.
- Alpha plus keyed by a date column with missing cells builds a different
  net around the `NaT` activity, and POWL keyed by such a column drops the
  traces whose cells are all `NaT`; Minera keeps them.
- On XES uploads pm4py's frame holds a date attribute as
  `datetime.datetime` objects in an object column, and Minera's errors name
  that type there too; where such an attribute sits beside text cells,
  pm4py's Inductive and POWL TypeError names the operands the other way
  round (`'<' not supported between instances of 'str' and
  'datetime.datetime'`; Minera `'datetime.datetime' and 'str'`).
- The case statistics' start and end on nanosecond cells (round BQ), the
  number-keyed DataFrame routes, the CSV timestamp columns of plain numbers
  and "roles to diagnostics groups" (round AT) stay as declared.

Verification (scripts in the project files under `review-harness/round-bs/`;
"before" is round BR's server on the same scripts):

| Check | Comparisons | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow miners keyed by the frame's typed columns (`typedkeys.py`: alpha, alpha plus, heuristics, Inductive, POWL; keys `act`, `concept:name`, an integer, a float with gaps, a date with gaps, text with blanks, a bool, `ts`, `time:timestamp`, `@@index`, the case column) | 1,650 on 30 CSV uploads, 700 on 20 XES uploads | before (10 CSV uploads): 274 of 550 differed; after: 33 and 23 differ, all declared (blank float or text keys, alpha plus and POWL on dates with `NaT`), the rest equal or raise the same TypeError |
| Petri comparison on the POWL and Inductive models, CSV with its own headers vs the same rows as XES (`cmpxes.py`) | 20 | before: every POWL comparison raised `KeyError: 'concept:name'`; after: all the same |
| Model routes on the POWL and imported models keyed by the header vs `concept:name` (`indkeys2.py`, 36 route variants) | 720 | all the same, 2 multi-alignments fail alike |
| LLM abstractions on nanosecond uploads vs pm4py (`llmns.py`: DFG, variants, event stream, log attributes, log features) | 200 on 40 uploads, and 200 on 40 fresh ones | before (30 uploads): 56 of 150 differed; after: all equal, 11 raise alike |
| Stochastic map (fitted timing) vs pm4py (round BR's `smapns.py`, 30 uploads and 30 fresh ones) | 60 | before: 5 failed on the reachability analysis; after: all maps returned and equal |
| XES uploads with sub-microsecond dates vs the same dates truncated (`xesns.py`: mine body, performance DFG, case statistics, sojourn time, interval tree, stochastic map, passed time) | 140 | all the same (the mine bodies apart from the upload's own name and size) |
| Service time, cycle time and case arrival on nanosecond cells vs pm4py (`perfns.py` with `NS=1`, 30 uploads) | 270 | all equal, 39 raise alike |
| Multipart parts on query-only routes (contract test and probes) | 30 routes | a part besides the uploads is rejected; query-string controls unchanged |
| Full suites: ctest, script tests, frontend tests, fixture replay | 477 ctests, 406 script tests, 10,729 frontend tests, 2,673 responses of 16 manifests | all pass; no fixture changed |

`minera_review_bs1_tests` binds the typed activity keys (alpha labels,
heuristics, Inductive and POWL errors), the LLM abstractions on a CSV with
nanosecond cells and the stochastic map without a CTMC;
`minera_server_parameter_contract_tests` binds the multipart rejection on
DFG precision and an OCEL route.

## Review BT1: re-review of round BS, typed columns as activity keys of the DFG variants, the DataFrame DFG, the LLM abstractions and the start/end and variant statistics, and unknown fields on the replay and model upload routes (2026-11-13)

Round BT checked BS's CI run (43347116082: all jobs green), re-reviewed BS
(the miners keyed by the frame's typed columns, the POWL Petri comparison on
a CSV upload's own headers and the LLM abstractions on nanosecond cells: on
fresh seeds only BS's declared differences remain) and took BS's targets:
typed activity keys on the DFG routes, the LLM abstractions and the
statistics families, the replay and alignment upload routes' unknown
fields, and the LLM abstractions on XES uploads. The device check on the
Mac was skipped (no device linked). Findings, all fixed:

- **BT1-1 Typed columns as the activity key of the DFG variants.**
  `/api/discover-dfg` (and the mine route's DFG variants) keyed by a typed
  column of a CSV or XES upload's frame kept the cell's text. pm4py's
  native, frequency-triples and causal variants (on `convert_to_event_log`)
  name an activity `str()` of the typed cell (`007` is `7`, a float `2` is
  `2.0`, a date its UTC `Timestamp`, a missing cell `nan` or `NaT`). The
  CLEAN variant on the frame splits a case into runs at a missing key cell
  (each run gives a start, an end and its inner pairs) and its shifted
  target column turns an int64 key into floats (`2 -> 1.0`). CLEAN_TIME
  raises `TypeError: dtype datetime64[s] cannot be converted to
  timedelta64[ns]` on a missing key cell and `ValueError: The column label
  'time:timestamp' is not unique.` keyed by the timestamp; its means are
  pandas' groupby means of int64 units (microseconds, nanoseconds once a
  cell has sub-microsecond digits; Kahan summation, truncated toward zero),
  which also corrects the default key on fractional timestamps. The
  performance variant, pm4py's `discover_performance_dfg` on the frame,
  checks the key column first (`the activity column should be of type
  string.`, then `the activity column should not contain any empty
  value.`). The analysis registers every label it returns, so a typed label
  no longer fails the graph lookup. On 10 uploads, 11 keys and 7 variants,
  415 of 770 answers differed.
- **BT1-2 The DataFrame DFG on typed keys.** `/api/dfg-dataframe` (pandas
  `get_dfg_graph`) names an activity `str()` of the frame's typed cell and
  its target through `shift()`, so an int64 key's targets are floats; Minera
  kept the text. On 10 uploads, 106 of 220 answers differed. The pandas
  adapter now reads the upload's frame (`csv_frame_cell_label`).
- **BT1-3 The LLM abstractions keyed by a column.** `/api/llm-context` with
  `activity_attribute` projected the events and dropped the frame, so on
  every CSV upload `concept:name`, the upload's activity, case and
  timestamp columns and any column with a blank raised `context activity
  attribute is absent or null`, and the other keys gave the events' text.
  pm4py's `abstract_dfg` keyed by a column is the DataFrame DFG of BT1-2
  (pairs with a missing cell dropped); `abstract_variants` raises
  `TypeError: sequence item N: expected str instance, T found` at the first
  cell that is no `str`, or, when two variants tie on count and
  performance, the `'<' not supported` TypeError of its sort comparing a
  text with a NaN (the variants in case order, CPython's list.sort);
  `abstract_event_stream` and `abstract_log_attributes` list the frame
  whatever the key; `abstract_log_features` reads the key as its activity
  (value and succession features). A key that names no column raises
  pandas' KeyError (`"['x'] not in index"` for the DFG, `'Column not found:
  x'` for the variants). On 10 uploads, 9 keys and 5 abstractions, 15 of 450
  answers were equal.
- **BT1-4 The features descriptions' budget.** pm4py's log and OCEL
  features descriptions stop once the text reaches `max_len`; Minera added
  one more line when the text was exactly `max_len` long (10 of 11 line
  boundaries on one upload).
- **BT1-5 Start/end activities and variant statistics keyed by a column.**
  pm4py's `get_start_activities`, `get_end_activities` and `get_variants`
  on an upload's frame check the key column as BT1-1's performance variant
  does, and read the upload's own case column; Minera counted every key's
  text (BK1 declared the column check) and returned nothing for the case
  column. On 10 uploads and 10 keys, 158 of 200 answers differed. Both
  routes (and the CLI) now go through `frame_activity_column_error` and the
  keyed frame (`discover_boundary_activities_as_uploaded`).
- **BT1-6 Unknown fields on the replay and model upload routes.**
  `/api/token-replay`, `/api/replay-token-workbench`,
  `/api/align-petri-workbench` and `/api/replay-fitness` read their controls
  from either the form or the query string and ignored any other name;
  `/api/check-model` and `/api/compare-petri` ignored names outside their
  controls. A misspelled control was dropped silently; the four routes now
  refuse a name none of their parsers consulted (`unknown or inapplicable
  <route> field: <name>`) and the other two refuse names outside their
  lists. `/api/compare-petri` read `initial_marking` and `final_marking`
  from the query string only, so the markings the client sends as form
  fields were dropped; it now reads both.
- **BT1-7 Replay fitness on a CSV upload's own headers.**
  `/api/replay-fitness` replayed `concept:name`, which a CSV upload with its
  own headers holds under the header, so every such replay raised
  `KeyError: 'concept:name'`; an omitted `evaluation_activity_attribute`
  now follows the upload's activity column as `/api/token-replay` does
  (equal to pm4py's `fitness_token_based_replay` on the frame).

Declarations:

- BS's float NaN declaration holds for the DFG variants too: pm4py's
  EventLog holds each blank of a float column (and, on an XES upload, a
  string attribute written as a float NaN) as its own object, so the
  native, triples and causal variants give each blank event its own `nan`
  activity; Minera labels them one `nan`.
- `abstract_log_features` raises `could not convert string to float` in
  pm4py only, on every key, under some hash seeds (AQ's declaration of
  string keys with gaps typed as numbers by set order).
- Not swept: the `clean_polars` variant keyed by a typed column, the LLM
  context's other variants (case, Declare, log skeleton, temporal profile,
  Petri net) keyed by a column and any variant with both an activity and a
  timestamp attribute (these keep the projection of the events).
- Still open: the session routes that read their controls from the query
  string, such as `/api/align`, ignore unknown parameters.
- The case statistics' start and end on nanosecond cells (round BQ), the
  CSV timestamp columns of plain numbers and "roles to diagnostics groups"
  (round AT) stay as declared.

Verification (scripts in the project files under `review-harness/round-bt/`;
"before" is round BS's server on the same scripts):

| Check | Comparisons | Result |
|---|---|---|
| DFG variants keyed by the frame's typed columns (`dfgkeys.py`: native, performance, frequency triples, clean, clean time, alpha and heuristic causal; keys `act`, `concept:name`, an integer, a float with gaps, a date with gaps, text with blanks, a bool, `ts`, `time:timestamp`, `@@index`, the case column) | 1,540 on 20 CSV uploads, 1,176 on 24 XES uploads | before (10 CSV uploads): 415 of 770 differed; after: 1,304 and 955 equal, 222 and 192 raise alike, 14 and 29 differ (declared float NaN) |
| DataFrame DFG keyed by the frame's typed columns (`dfgdfkeys.py`, frequency and performance) | 440 on 20 uploads | before (10 uploads): 106 of 220 differed; after: all equal |
| LLM abstractions keyed by a column (`llmkeys.py`: DFG, variants, event stream, log attributes, log features) | 3,780 on 132 CSV uploads, 600 on 20 XES uploads | before (10 uploads): 15 of 450 equal; after: equal or raising alike with the same message, apart from AQ's hash-seed feature error (pm4py only, 9 on one CSV upload, 24 on XES) |
| Start/end activities and variant statistics keyed by the frame's columns (`statkeys.py`) | 800 on 40 CSV uploads, 560 on 40 XES uploads | before (10 uploads): 158 of 200 differed; after: all equal (errors with pm4py's message) |
| Features budget at each line boundary (`budgetprobe.py`, `ocelbudget.py`: DFG, variants, event stream, log features, OCEL features) | 41 | before: 10 of 11 log-feature boundaries differed; after: all equal |
| Unknown fields on the six upload routes, compare-petri markings, replay fitness on own headers (contract test and probes) | 6 routes | unknown names refused, known controls unchanged; replay fitness equal to pm4py |
| Re-review of BS: `typedkeys.py` (15 uploads), `cmpxes.py` (15), `llmns.py` (15) | 915 | only BS's declared differences (blank float and text keys, alpha plus and POWL on `NaT`) |
| Full suites: ctest, script tests, frontend tests, fixture replay | 478 ctests, 406 script tests, 10,729 frontend tests, 2,673 responses of 16 manifests | all pass; no fixture changed |

## Review BU1: re-review of round BT, unknown parameters on the query-string session routes, the LLM model descriptions keyed by a column and the OCEL abstractions on nanosecond timestamps (2026-11-13)

Round BU checked BT's CI run (43358535741: the Python, verifier, frontend
and macOS jobs green, Linux and Windows ctest still running at the time of
writing), re-reviewed BT (the DFG variants, the DataFrame DFG, the LLM
abstractions and the statistics keyed by typed columns: on fresh seeds only
BT's declared differences remain) and took BT's targets. Findings, all
fixed:

- **BU1-1 The LLM model descriptions keyed by a column.**
  `/api/llm-context`'s `log_skeleton`, `declare` and `temporal_profile`
  variants with `activity_attribute` set projected the events, so on a CSV
  upload every key that is no plain event attribute (the upload's own
  activity, case and timestamp columns, `case:concept:name`) raised
  `context activity attribute is absent or null`, and the typed columns
  described their text. pm4py's `discover_log_skeleton`, `discover_declare`
  and `discover_temporal_profile` on the upload's frame check the key as a
  DataFrame activity column: a name outside the frame raises `the specified
  activity column is not contained in the dataframe. Available columns:
  [...]` (the frame's columns, sorted), a column of another dtype `the
  activity column should be of type string.`, a column with a blank `the
  activity column should not contain any empty value.`; otherwise the
  column's text is the activity (the case column too, so each case holds
  one activity). The temporal profile keyed by `case:concept:name` fails on
  its merge (`KeyError: "['case:concept:name_2'] not in index"`). On 25
  uploads, 9 keys and 3 variants, 90 of 675 answers were equal or raised
  alike before; all are now.
- **BU1-2 The OCEL features description's lifecycle paths.**
  `pm4py.llm.abstract_ocel_features` extracts the object features with the
  lifecycle path features on (`Frequency of the path "A" -> "B" in the
  lifecycle of the object`), which the feature extraction's own default
  leaves off; Minera left them off. `/api/llm-context`'s `ocel_features`
  now follows `include_lifecycle_paths` (default on, as pm4py). Before, 44
  of 60 answers on OCEL 1.0 and 2.0 JSON differed.
- **BU1-3 The OCEL events and objects text on nanosecond timestamps.**
  `pm4py.llm.abstract_ocel` on `read_ocel_json` / `read_ocel2_json` prints
  each timestamp as pandas' `str(Timestamp)` of the UTC microseconds
  (`2029-05-12 06:16:59.641000+00:00`, no fraction on a whole second; the
  nanosecond digits are dropped), orders the events by timestamp, then
  activity, then id, prints the lifecycle duration as a Python float of
  the seconds between those microseconds, and joins the object lines
  without a final newline. Minera printed the texts' milliseconds, kept the
  file's order on ties and ended with a newline: every `ocel` answer
  differed.
- **BU1-4 Unknown parameters on the query-string session routes.**
  `/api/align`, `/api/evaluate`, `/api/evaluate-emd`, `/api/playout` (GET
  and POST), `/api/petri-analysis`, `/api/reduce-process-tree` and the GET
  exports `/api/pnml`, `/api/bpmn`, `/api/ptml` and `/api/xes` read their controls
  from the query string and ignored any other name, so a misspelled control
  was dropped silently (`traces` on a DFG playout, `miner` on the Petri
  analysis, whose selector is `petri_analysis_miner`). Each read now goes
  through the form field audit of BT1-6, and a successful answer is
  replaced with 400 `unknown or inapplicable <route> parameter: <name>`
  when a parameter or file part was never consulted.

Declarations:

- `clean_polars` keyed by any column is unreachable in pm4py on the pinned
  polars 1.44.1: `CLEAN_POLARS` calls `DataFrame.with_column`, which this
  polars no longer has, and a `LazyFrame` is not subscriptable, so nothing
  compares; Minera keeps its own polars-free result.
- The LLM context's `case` variant stays Minera's own log projection
  (docs/case-description-audit.md); keyed by a column it is not a parity
  target.
- BT's float NaN declaration (each blank its own `nan` object) and AQ's
  hash-seed `could not convert string to float` in `abstract_log_features`
  reconfirmed on fresh seeds.
- Not swept, moved to round BV: the log filter bank
  (`/api/reference-log-filter`, `/api/reference-log-attributes`) on typed
  XES attributes and the `/api/reference-table-*` routes on typed native
  EventTable JSON inputs. The attribute and case statistics keyed by typed
  columns were covered in rounds AU and AX.
- The case statistics' start and end on nanosecond cells (round BQ), the
  CSV timestamp columns of plain numbers and "roles to diagnostics groups"
  (round AT) stay as declared.

Verification (scripts in the project files under `review-harness/round-bu/`;
"before" is round BT's server on the same scripts):

| Check | Comparisons | Result |
|---|---|---|
| LLM model descriptions keyed by the frame's columns (`llmkeys2.py`: log skeleton, Declare, temporal profile; keys `act`, `concept:name`, an integer, a float with gaps, a date with gaps, text with blanks, a bool, the case column, `ts`) | 675 on 25 CSV uploads, 180 more on 15 uploads keyed by `case:concept:name`, `@@case_index`, `@@index`, `time:timestamp`, 270 on 10 fresh uploads, 240 on 10 XES uploads | before: 90 of 675 equal or raising alike; after: all equal (relation lines in set order compare as sets) or raising alike with pm4py's message |
| OCEL abstractions on nanosecond timestamps (`ocelllm.py`: `ocel`, `ocel_ocdfg`, `ocel_features`) | 450 on 150 OCEL 1.0/2.0 JSON files, 160 features answers with a random lifecycle paths flag | before: every `ocel` answer and 44 of 60 features answers differed; after: all equal |
| Unknown query parameters on the ten session routes (contract test; every other route that reads the query already checks an allow list) | 10 routes | unknown names refused, known controls and the routes' own errors unchanged |
| Re-review of BT on fresh seeds: `dfgkeys.py`, `dfgdfkeys.py`, `statkeys.py` (round BT's scripts) | 1,200, 880 and 1,200 | all equal or raising alike with pm4py's message |

## Review BV1: re-review of round BU, the log filter bank on typed XES attributes, the LLM context with a timestamp attribute and the OCEL edge timings on nanosecond timestamps (2026-11-13)

Round BV checked BU's CI run (43367732932: green on all six jobs),

against the frontend's parameter combinations, the `FrameKeyScope`
argument, the lifecycle path features: no regressions) and took BU's

  and the typed columns timed nothing. pm4py.llm on the upload's frame

  time datetime. Use the function pandas.to_datetime`, `the timestamp
  column should not contain any empty value.`) and the temporal profile

- **BV1-2 The trace and start activity filters' errors.**

## Review BW1: re-review of round BV, the table filter routes on typed EventTable JSON, and the OCEL filter, features and exports on nanosecond timestamps (2026-11-13)

Round BW checked BV's CI run (43375436443: green on all six jobs),
re-reviewed BV (`frame_timestamp_context`, `frame_stream_ranks`,
`discover_temporal_profile_frame`, the trace filter's `python_type`: no
regressions) and took BV's targets. Findings, all fixed:

- **BW1-1 Polars Datetime columns of ns and ms units on the table filters.**
  The native Polars filters behind `/api/reference-table-*` (timestamp,
  cases, variants, paths, between, LTL, attributes) refused every
  `Datetime(time_unit='ns'|'ms', ...)` column (`Unsupported native Polars
  ... dtype`). pm4py's Polars filters run on them: a cell holds its column
  unit; Polars 1.44.1 compares a Datetime column with the microsecond
  literal of a Python datetime by flooring the bound to a millisecond
  column, while on a nanosecond column `<=` and `==` floor the cell to
  microseconds and `>` and `!=` compare the exact nanoseconds (`>=` and `<`
  agree either way), so the events and contained filters keep a cell
  600 ns after the upper bound and the intersecting filter treats it as
  after the bound; a naive column's `SchemaError` names its unit
  (`Datetime('ns')`, `Datetime('ms')`); case and path durations count the
  whole seconds of the column unit (truncated); grouping keys and orders
  use the column unit; a numeric bound meets a Datetime column's physical
  ticks of its unit; `is_in` errors print the column dtype with its zone
  (`Datetime('ns', 'UTC')`). The shared rules are in
  `src/backend/polars_datetime.hpp`. Before, 480 of 1,080 Polars answers on
  ns and ms columns were equal or raised alike.
- **BW1-2 pandas paths on nanosecond timestamps.** The pandas paths and
  path performance filters ordered a case's events by microseconds, so two
  events of one microsecond kept their row order; pandas sorts the
  `datetime64[ns]` column by the exact instant (`pandas_paths_filter.cpp`).
  Before, 8 of 120 paths and path performance answers differed.
- **BW1-3 The OCEL SQLite export on nanosecond timestamps.**
  `/api/ocel/sqlite?mode=export` wrote the event times (and the object
  change times and typed timestamp attributes) with their nanoseconds;
  pm4py's `write_ocel2_sqlite` writes them through Python datetimes, the
  nanoseconds floored to microseconds (`2033-06-07
  06:41:59.593824+00:00`). Before, the event times of all 25 files
  differed.
- **BW1-4 The OCEL features on nanosecond timestamps.**
  `/api/ocel/features` read a nanosecond event time as a double of the
  exact instant for `@@event_timestamp`, the lifecycle start, end and
  duration and the prefix time differences; pm4py reads
  `Timestamp.timestamp()`, the epoch seconds rounded to microseconds
  (2001739319.593824). Before, 24 of 25 event and 25 of 32 object
  comparisons differed.

Declarations:

- Polars sorts a case's events by case and timestamp with an unstable
  sort: on some frames events with equal timestamps leave their row order
  (deterministic, independent of the thread count). Minera sorts stably.
  The paths, path performance and variants filters then differ on those
  frames (4 of 1,440 answers on us and ns columns, 2 of 1,080 on us
  columns; present before this round). Moved to round BX.
- The LLM context's timestamp attribute on XES uploads with date
  attributes that have gaps behaves as BV's declared CSV gap case (the DFG
  and variants keep the projection and raise `context timestamp attribute
  is absent or null`).
- pm4py's Polars `filter_variants_from_list` (`var_from_list`) raises
  `AttributeError: module 'pm4py.util.constants' has no attribute
  'DEFAULT_NAME_KEY'` on polars 1.44.1; Minera raises the same.
- Polars `between` row order and `filter_on_ncases` case choice vary per
  run in Polars itself (the harness compares them as sets).
- The non-exact `timestamp` variant of `/api/ocel/filter` is Minera's own
  lenient bound parser; `timestamp_exact` is the pm4py one (equal on all
  360 comparisons).

Tests: `minera_review_bw1_tests` (values taken from pm4py on the same
frames and OCEL, `review-harness/round-bw/bw1/mk.py`).

| Polars table filters on us and ns columns (`tbl.py --eng=polars --units=us,ns` and `--units=us`) | 1,440 and 1,080 | all equal or raising alike except the declared sort ties (4 and 2) |

## Review BX1: re-review of round BW, Polars' unstable sort of tied timestamps, temporal and Boolean columns as keys and attributes of the Polars table filters, and the OCEL description on nanosecond timestamps (2026-11-13)

Round BX checked BW's CI run (43384361792: green on all six jobs),
re-reviewed BW (`polars_datetime.hpp` and its callers, the pandas paths
`compare`, `ocel_features` `event_times`, the SQLite `microseconds` flag:
no regressions) and took BW's targets. Findings, all fixed:

- **BX1-1 Polars' unstable sort of tied timestamps.** The native Polars
  paths, path performance, variants, between, LTL and sequence filters
  sorted a frame by case and timestamp stably. Polars 1.44.1 sorts by
  several columns with rayon's parallel unstable sort (a port of the Rust
  pdqsort: insertion sort up to 20 rows, median-of-three and ninther
  pivots, BlockQuicksort partitions of 128-row blocks, an equal-run split
  when the pivot equals the slice's predecessor, xorshift pattern breaking
  after an imbalanced split, both sides recursed afresh when the larger
  exceeds 2,000 rows). The order it leaves tied rows in is deterministic
  and does not depend on the thread count. `src/backend/polars_sort.hpp`
  reproduces it; the model matched Polars on 2,000 random frames of 21 to
  4,100 rows (ties, nulls, string and integer first keys). A key of the
  `Null` dtype (an all-null column) drops out of the sort, and the
  single-column sort that remains keeps tied rows in their input order
  (`sort_by_keys`; 700 random frames, and the retained LTL vector
  PLTL-B1-130). Before, 12 and 7 of 5,000 answers on us and ns columns
  differed (BW's declared ties).
- **BX1-2 Polars Datetime and Date columns as activity keys.** The paths
  and variants filters read a Datetime activity through its String cast
  with the microsecond text of the cell; Polars prints the column unit's
  fraction digits (9, 6 or 3) and, on an aware column, the "+HH:MM" offset
  (`2024-01-01 00:00:00.000000001+00:00`); a Date prints `2024-01-01`
  (`polars_datetime::cast_text`).
- **BX1-3 Polars top_k with the activity key on the case column.**
  `filter_variants_top_k` with `activity_key` equal to `case_id_key` fails
  resolving the group_by with `DuplicateError: column with name '<case>'
  has more than one occurrence` and the sort plan; Minera returned rows.
- **BX1-4 The Polars timestamp attribute filter on Boolean, temporal and
  nanosecond columns.** A Boolean attribute compared with a string value
  matches through `col(b).cast(String) == "true"` (Minera matched
  nothing); a Date or Datetime attribute with a string value raises
  `InvalidOperationError: cannot compare 'date/datetime/time' to a string
  value ...` resolving the join; on an aware nanosecond time column the
  error expressions print the `<=` bound 999 ns on
  (`2024-01-02 00:00:00.000000999 UTC`) and equal bounds stay a range
  instead of `==`.
- **BX1-5 The OCEL description on nanosecond timestamps.**
  `/api/ocel/description` printed event and lifecycle times as ISO texts
  and the lifecycle duration from the exact instants; pm4py prints
  `str(Timestamp)` (`2033-06-07 06:41:59.593824219+00:00`) and the float
  repr of `end.timestamp() - start.timestamp()` (microseconds, rounded:
  `90179.00005412102`).

Declarations:

- With non-default case, activity and timestamp keys, Polars' join and
  group_by results (case performance and size, contained and
  intersecting, repetition, top_k, attribute traces) change row order from
  run to run in Polars itself (26 of 5,400 answers; the same seed
  reorders when rerun). The harness reports them as `ORDER`.
- The native description variant2 objects carry a `has_lifecycle` flag
  before the lifecycle fields (Minera's wire shape for objects without
  events); the harness drops it.
- The pandas filters with non-default keys (numbers, booleans or dates as
  activities, the case key on the timestamp column, null case keys, a
  datetime attribute against a string) show differences in error texts
  and in a few answers; moved to round BY.

## Review BY1: re-review of round BX, the pandas table filters with non-default keys, and the OCEL routes on nanosecond SQLite timestamps (2026-11-13)

Round BY checked BX's CI run (43393668614: green), re-reviewed BX
(`polars_sort.hpp` line by line against rayon's pdqsort, its callers and
`sort_by_keys` on 11 key dtypes, `polars_datetime::cast_text`, top_k's
`DuplicateError`, `nanosecond_aware` and `at_most_text`, the OCEL
`description_time`: no regressions; 2,000 Polars tie answers and 600 Polars
LTL tie answers equal) and took BX's targets. Findings, all fixed:

- **BY1-1 Vectorised concatenation errors of the pandas paths filters.**
  The paths and path performance filters build `col + ","` over the
  activity column, so pandas raises by the column's dtype, also on an
  empty frame: `UFuncTypeError: ufunc 'add' did not contain a loop with
  signature matching types (dtype('int64'), dtype('<U1')) -> None` for
  numpy bool, integer, float and complex columns (nullable `Int64`,
  `boolean`, `Float64` under their numpy names), and `TypeError:
  unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'DatetimeArray' and 'str'` (also
  `TimedeltaArray`, `PeriodArray`, `Categorical`). Minera matched the
  cells' texts or raised its own message.
- **BY1-2 Path performance with the case key on the activity or
  timestamp column** raises `ValueError: Can only compare
  identically-labeled (both index and columns) DataFrame objects`.
- **BY1-3 Case performance with the case key on the timestamp column**
  raises `ValueError: Grouper for 'time:timestamp' not 1-dimensional`.
- **BY1-4 A string against a datetime column** (timestamp attribute
  filter, repetition filter): pandas parses the text as a Timestamp and
  compares instants; the texts it reads as NaT (`NaT`, `nat`, `NAT`,
  `NaN`, `nan`, `NAN`, empty) match no cell, a naive text on an aware
  column takes the column's zone, an aware text never equals a naive
  column (`pandas_datetime_target.hpp`). Minera compared texts.
- **BY1-5 Missing case values and activities on top_k and coverage.**
  The variants come from `np.unique(..., return_index, return_counts)`
  runs over the case column: typed arrays (float, integer, bool, naive
  `datetime64`) sort NaN/NaT last and collapse them into one run; object
  arrays (objects, aware `datetime64` as Timestamps) sort with Python's
  comparisons (numpy's object timsort): `None` or mixed types raise
  `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of ...`, NaN and NaT
  compare unordered and each stays its own run. The coverage denominator
  counts the non-missing case ids; variants whose activities hold a NaN or
  NaT handed out fresh by numpy (float and naive `datetime64` columns)
  never equal another, and comparing variants of mixed item types raises.
  Minera raised `'<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' ...`
  on every missing case value.
- **BY1-6 Between on datetime case columns.** Naive `datetime64` case
  values of every unit label the subcases with numpy's `str` at the unit's
  digits (`2024-01-01T00:00:00.000000` for us, none for s) and the NaT run
  `NaT`; an aware column with NaT takes the exact timsort order. On an
  object case column the error of a failing comparison names the operands
  in the order numpy's sort compares them at any length (Minera's own
  merge order for more than 16 rows).
- **BY1-7 The OCEL connected-component split** builds each component from
  its events, objects and relations only: pm4py drops O2O rows and object
  changes there (the ancestors/descendants split keeps them). Minera kept
  them.
- **BY1-8 OCEL SQLite relation order.** `read_ocel2_sqlite` keeps the
  `event_object` rows in row order and sorts them by time, stably, so the
  relations of events at one instant from different type tables keep the
  row order, unlike the events (which the reader takes by row place, then
  type). Minera sorted relations by their event's position. The lifecycle
  qualifiers (`/api/ocel/enrich`, now per relation row in relation order)
  and the DF edges of `/api/ocel/event-object-graph` follow the relation
  order. Relations of every reader now sort by their event's instant
  (stable), which equals the event position for the JSON, XML and CSV
  readers; the OCEL JSON transport (both forms) carries
  `"minera:relationOrder"` (each relation's event id in log order) when
  the log order differs from the nesting.
- **BY1-9 OCEL SQLite object change order.** pm4py takes the change rows
  of the object type tables by row place, then type, and sorts them by
  time; Minera kept table order, and the OCEL 2.0 transport (changes
  nested per object) lost any order. The event/object graph numbers its
  change nodes (`@@change##i`) in that order. The OCEL 2.0 transport now
  carries `"minera:objectChangeOrder"` (each change's object and field in
  log order) when the order a reader takes back differs.

Declarations:

- pandas membership of variant tuples whose naive `datetime64[ns]`
  activities hold sub-microsecond values depends on `PYTHONHASHSEED` in
  the reference (`np.datetime64` hashes such values with the seed, unlike
  the equal `Timestamp`); top_k and coverage answers on such columns
  change from seed to seed (6 of 16,000 answers). Minera answers as the
  seeds where the two hashes differ.
- A datetime column against a text outside ISO-8601 goes through pandas'
  dateutil fallback, which Minera does not reproduce (native error).
- pm4py orders the connected components by set iteration over object ids,
  which changes with `PYTHONHASHSEED` (2 of 300 logs); the harness
  compares them as a set.
- An OCEL SQLite file with repeated `event_object` rows loses the repeats
  through the OCEL 2.0 transport, which keeps one relation per event and
  object as `read_ocel2_json` does (OC2); moved to round BZ.

Tests: `minera_review_by1_tests` (values taken from pm4py on the same
frames and OCEL files, `review-harness/round-by/by1/mk.py` and
`by1/sqlitecase.py`).

## Review BZ1: re-review of round BY, repeated relations and row order of OCEL SQLite files through discovery, nullable and categorical keys of the pandas table filters, and the pandas LTL filters with non-default keys (2026-11-13)

Round BZ checked BY's CI run (43409678034) and BX's (43393668614): both green;
it re-reviewed BY (`pandas_datetime_target.hpp` on zones other than UTC,
offsets and units: 800 answers equal; BY's typed-key sweep on 300 seeds:
equal) and took BY's targets. Findings, all fixed:

- **BZ1-1 Repeated `event_object` rows through the OCEL transport.**
  `read_ocel2_sqlite` keeps an event's repeated rows for one object; the
  OCEL 2.0 JSON transport kept one relation per event and object (as
  `read_ocel2_json` does), the classic transport one per `ocel:omap`
  entry. Both forms now carry `"minera:repeatedRelations": true` when a
  log holds a repeat, and the readers then keep every listed relation.
- **BZ1-2 O2O row order across source objects.** pm4py keeps the
  `object_object` rows in row order; the OCEL 2.0 transport nests them
  per source object. It now carries `"minera:o2oOrder"` (each row's
  source id in log order) when the order differs from the nesting.
- **BZ1-3 OCDFG start and end activities on a tied log.** pm4py takes an
  object's start and end activities from its first and last relation row
  (relation order: rows sorted by time, stably), while the edges follow
  the event order. Minera took both from the event order.
- **BZ1-4 OCPN per-type logs.** Each object's trace is its relation rows,
  repeats kept, in event order. The classic inductive miner sorts each
  trace by time (stably); the token-based replay diagnostics read it as
  listed. With `inductive_miner_variant="imd"` the DFG edges come from the
  listed traces and the start and end activities from the relation rows'
  first and last activity. (On imported logs event order is time order,
  ties in file order; logs built in memory keep their own order.) Minera mined one event
  per (event, object) in event order. `/api/ocel/discover` takes the new
  `ocpn_variant` control (`log`/`im` or `dfg`/`imd`, as on the playout
  route), and the OCEL explorer has an "Inductive miner" selector for the
  OCPN model.
- **BZ1-5 SAW nets** mine (without the time sort) and weigh (token-replay
  firing counts) the same per-type traces as BZ1-4.
- **BZ1-6 Lifecycle qualifiers on repeated rows.** Per object, the first
  relation row labels its event `creation`, the last `termination`, the
  others `other`; an event with several rows for the object takes `other`
  when one of them is neither first nor last, otherwise `creation` before
  `termination` (all its rows get that label). Minera labelled each row by
  its own place.
- **BZ1-7 What NumPy reads from nullable and categorical columns.** pandas
  3 hands columns to NumPy through `to_numpy()`: a masked numeric column
  (`Int64`, `UInt8`, `Float64`, ...) with a gap becomes a float array
  holding NaN (without one, its NumPy dtype), `boolean` with a gap and
  `string` stay object arrays holding `<NA>`, a categorical column becomes
  its categories' array with NaN for a gap (float64 for numeric
  categories, a NaN object otherwise). The variants statistics (top_k,
  coverage: `np.unique` runs and variant tuples) and the between filter
  read case and activity columns so: an `Int64` case column with `<NA>`
  now groups its gap as one NaN run (pm4py returns results where Minera
  raised `boolean value of NA is ambiguous`), labels between subcases
  `1.0##@@0` and `nan##@@0`, and a categorical gap fails with `'<' not
  supported between instances of 'str' and 'float'` (Minera named
  `'NoneType'`).
- **BZ1-8 `isin` on a masked numeric case column never matches `<NA>`**,
  even when the selected cases hold one (`np.asarray` of the selection is
  a float array): the attributes filter on traces and the timestamp
  attribute filter keep `<NA>` case rows only when negative. A `boolean`
  or `string` case column matches `<NA>` when the selection holds it.
- **BZ1-9 The pandas LTL filters with duplicated role keys.** A resource
  key naming the case column fails first (`Cannot set a DataFrame with
  multiple columns to the single column @@conceptname`, also when all
  three keys are one column); with timestamp differences, a timestamp key
  on the activity column raises `cannot reindex on an axis with duplicate
  labels` and on the case column `The column label '<name>' is not
  unique.`
- **BZ1-10 Paths on interval and Sparse activity columns** raise the
  vectorised `col + ","` errors (`TypeError: unsupported operand type(s)
  for +: 'IntervalArray' and 'str'`; a `Sparse[T, fill]` column the
  `UFuncTypeError` of `T`).

Declarations:

- pm4py's O2O enrichment appends the computed graph links in set
  iteration order, which changes with `PYTHONHASHSEED`; the harness
  compares them as a multiset (Minera's order is deterministic).
- The merged SAW net is compared on structure: pm4py keeps one weight
  distribution per arc, Minera's JSON keeps each arc's (`arc_weights`)
  and their sum per merged transition; the per-type nets compare weights
  exactly.
- The table transport has no timedelta cell kind, so `timedelta64`
  columns cannot be keys or attributes of the table filters.
- The pandas sequence filters (start and end activities, prefixes,
  suffixes, rework, case grouping) have no HTTP route; their bank covers
  string and integer keys only (moved to round CA for typed keys).

frames and OCEL files, `review-harness/round-bz/probes/bz1.py`,
`bz1ocel.py`, `bz1ocel2.py`); the frontend test of the OCPN inductive miner

## Review CA1: re-review of round BZ, the pandas and Polars sequence filters with typed keys, the Polars table filters on narrow integer keys, and repeated OCEL relations in statistics, description and playout (2026-11-13)

Round CA checked BZ's CI run (43425776838): green on all six jobs. It
re-reviewed BZ (the pandas table filters with typed keys on 150 seeds and
the pandas LTL filters with typed keys on 1,500 answers: all equal or
raising alike) and took BZ's targets. Findings, all fixed:

- **CA1-1 pandas sequence filters on typed keys.** A new bank
  (`scripts/pandas_sequence_filter_typed_domain.py`: categorical case and
  activity columns with gaps, unused, integer, reversed and ordered
  categories, `Int64`, `UInt8`, `Float64`, `boolean`, `string` and object
  cases) found: the consecutive case grouping adds the key columns, which
  a categorical side refuses (`Object with dtype category cannot perform
  the numpy op add`, or `unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'Categorical'
  and 'DatetimeArray'` between two extension arrays), and a `string` key
  holds `<NA>`, whose comparison continues the run; the timestamp case
  grouping of two rows dropped the categorical descriptor of its first
  column; the variants statistics name a categorical gap `float` (`NaTType`
  for datetime categories); the activity split reads its case and
  activity columns as NumPy hands them; prefixes and suffixes on a
  categorical activity compare categories (the comparison error when no
  category is missing or repeated, null otherwise); the end activity
  counts give a missing key `None` on object columns and NaN otherwise;
  `filter_df_on_end_activities_nocc` raises `boolean value of NA is
  ambiguous` when a `<NA>` end activity below the threshold meets the most
  common variant.
- **CA1-2 Polars sequence filters on Categorical, Enum and narrow keys.**
  A new bank (`scripts/polars_sequence_filter_typed_domain.py`) found:
  the trace filter and `get_variants_df` join each case's activity list,
  which only a String column can (`attempted list join with non-string
  dtype: list[enum]`, `list[cat]`, `list[i64]`, ...); `is_in` with str
  values on an Enum column casts them strictly (``conversion from `str` to
  `enum` failed in column '' for N out of M values: [...]``, the first ten
  failures printed as Polars prints a short Series) in the start and end
  activity filters, `filter_df_on_end_activities` and its `nocc` form,
  the rework activity set (before the case column is resolved) and the
  activity split; the join key SchemaError names dtypes as Polars does
  (`bool`, `u8`, `f64`, `enum`, `cat`, `datetime[μs, UTC]`), the trace
  filter's case list takes the dtype of its Python values (ints `i64`,
  floats `f64`, bools `bool`, Categorical and Enum values `str`) and an
  integer case of any width joins it; a prefix or suffix list cast to an
  Enum activity turns values outside the categories into nulls, and a
  null item matches a null activity; the variants sort an Enum case by
  category position, Float64 by value (NaN last) and Boolean false first;
  the variants frames keep the case column's Categorical or Enum
  descriptor.
- **CA1-3 Polars table filters on narrow integer keys.** The case,
  paths, variants, between, timestamp, attributes and LTL filters refused
  `UInt8` (and `Int8`, `Int16`, `UInt16`) columns as "unsupported native
  dtype"; they now treat every integer width as an integer key, and the
  timestamp attribute filter names it in `cannot compare string with
  numeric type (u8)`.
- **CA1-4 OCEL edge metrics on repeated relations.** pm4py keeps an
  event's repeated `event_object` rows, so the object's sequence repeats
  the event and gives a self-edge (`b->b` with `(e3, e3, o1)`); Minera
  deduplicated the rows.
- **CA1-5 OCEL description on repeated relations** lists the object again
  (`related objects: o1, o1`).
- **CA1-6 OCPN playout without `max_traces`.** pm4py's extensive playout
  returns every complete sequence; the reference binding of
  `/api/ocel/playout` cut the result at the native default of 100 traces.
  It now keeps them all unless `max_traces` is given (explicit values keep
  the 10,000 safety bound).

Declarations:

- pandas `rework.apply` with both keys missing lists them in a Python set's

  the reverse), which changes with `PYTHONHASHSEED`; the bank keeps both.

## Review CB1: re-review of round CA, the reference OCPN playout's speed, the pandas sequence filters on `datetime64` keys, and the Polars sequence filters on temporal and integer activities (2026-11-13)

Round CB checked CA's CI run (43473813818): green on all six jobs. It
re-reviewed CA (fresh seeds of both typed sequence filter domains and the
OCEL association statistics with repeated relations: all equal, see the
table) and took CA's targets. Findings, all fixed:

- **CB1-1 OCPN playout speed and size.** The reference search behind
  `/api/ocel/playout` (pm4py's extensive variant) explored the same dead
  ends again on logs with repeated relations: seed 35 of the round-CA
  OCEL sweep (756,756 complete sequences of 15 silent steps) took 647 s,
  pm4py 81 s. The search now remembers states from which no complete
  sequence is reachable and skips them (5.6 s, the same traces), visits
  each complete sequence without keeping the whole list, and the route
  converts each trace to the OCEL result as it is found and stops the
  search once `max_traces` traces are kept (the first ones in search
  order, as the cut of the full list kept). A log with 5,187,076
  sequences that ran out of memory under a 2.5 GB limit now finishes in
  24 s.
- **CB1-2 pandas sequence filters on `datetime64` keys.** A new bank
  (`scripts/pandas_sequence_filter_cb_domain.py`: `datetime64` case and
  activity columns in us, ns, UTC and Europe/Berlin ms, with NaT; `int64`
  and `Int64` activities) found: the consecutive case grouping adds the
  case and activity columns, and a `datetime64` side raises by the other
  side's dtype (`cannot add DatetimeArray and DatetimeArray`, the integer
  addition message of `DatetimeArray`, NumPy's `ufunc 'add' cannot use
  operands with types dtype('<M8[us]') and dtype('float64')` for a naive
  column and a float one, `Could not convert object to NumPy datetime`
  for a Boolean one, elementwise `Timestamp`/`NaTType` errors for an
  aware column, and for str, `string` and object partners an error that
  depends on how many rows hold both values); the activity split sorts a
  naive `datetime64` case column as NumPy does (NaT last, all NaT one run)
  and an aware one as objects (NaT never equal), labels runs as NumPy and
  pandas print them, and a `datetime64` activity column matches no str or
  int argument; on naive `datetime64[ns]` keys the rework filter's kept
  cases come back as integers and never match, and the `nocc` filter's
  kept activities never match unless all are kept; a missing datetime key
  counts as `None` in the end activity counts and never matches a
  `None`/NaN boundary value; a missing value of a masked numeric end
  activity column becomes a NaN key (CA1-1's `boolean value of NA is
  ambiguous` holds only for `boolean` and `string` columns).
- **CB1-3 Polars sequence filters on `Int64`, `UInt8`, `Date` and
  `Datetime` activities.** A new bank
  (`scripts/polars_sequence_filter_cb_domain.py`) found: Polars builds
  the activity arguments into a Series as it builds a Python list (the
  first value's type decides when the others fit it, else a strict
  rebuild raises `unexpected value while building Series of type Int64;
  found value of type String: "a"` with its hint), and `is_in` refuses a
  list it cannot compare (`'is_in' cannot check for List(String) values in
  Datetime('μs') data`, `... in Date data`, `... in Int64 data`), the
  resolved plan showing Polars' casts (`col("concept:name").cast(Int64)`
  on a `UInt8` column, `.strict_cast(Float64)` for a float list); the
  variant strings of `starts_with`, `ends_with` and `get_variants_df`
  cast the activities to String (`2021-01-03 03:00:00`, aware ones in
  their zone with the offset); prefix and suffix lists are cast to the
  activity dtype without strictness (unparsable or out-of-range values
  become null, and null matches null), `starts_with` joins every item
  with `","` (`sequence item 0: expected str instance, int found`),
  `ends_with` joins only when the first item is a list or tuple, and the
  trace filter reads its items as str (`decoding to str: need a
  bytes-like object, int found`); the end activity counts hand out
  Python values (`datetime.date`, `datetime.datetime` in microseconds,
  ints); a Python datetime list is in microseconds, so on a nanosecond
  column `is_in` compares the raw numbers (the `nocc` filter keeps
  nothing) and a millisecond column refuses it (`'is_in' cannot check
  for Microseconds precision values in Milliseconds Datetime data`, the
  plan printing the values in the column's zone with its abbreviation,
  `2021-03-24 04:00:00.004 CET`); plans print lists of more than three
  values as Polars does (the first two, `…`, the last).

Declarations:

- pandas `rework.apply` with both keys missing (Python set order) as in
  CA; the CB bank keeps both orders of its two such calls.
- Polars per-run row orders of the consecutive case grouping with null
  activities: the CB bank runs each call eight times per hash seed and
  compares those calls up to row order (three runs per seed missed three
  of them).
- The membership error of the pandas filters is spelled `argument of
  type 'int' is not a container or iterable` on Python 3.14 (the
  reviewer's runtime) and `... is not iterable` on 3.11; Minera follows
  3.14 and the bank test accepts the 3.11 spelling of the capture.
- OCPN playout with `max_bindings_per_activity=2` still explodes on some
  logs on both sides (24 of 239 such runs did not finish within 40 s and
  2.5 GB on either side).

banks replayed by `minera_pandas_sequence_filter_cb_bank_parity_tests` and

## Review CC1: re-review of round CB, more `datetime64` keys and datetime arguments in the pandas sequence filters, and temporal and narrow numeric arguments in the Polars sequence filters (2026-11-13)

Round CC checked CB's CI run (43495896217): five jobs green, the Windows
job failed one test. It re-reviewed CB on fresh seeds of both CB domains
and took CB's targets. Findings, all fixed:

- **CC1-1 Zone abbreviations on Windows.** The Polars CB bank failed on
  MSVC in seven `filter_df_on_end_activities_nocc` calls: their plans
  print the activity values in the column's zone, and MSVC's zone
  database names Europe/Berlin's winter offset `GMT+1` where Polars prints
  `CET` (the ICU abbreviations declared in Review AY2). On MSVC the bank
  test now compares a second time with the word after each datetime's
  wall clock masked; elsewhere the abbreviations must match exactly.
- **CC1-2 Float keys of masked integer end activities (re-review of
  CB).** A fresh seed of the pandas CB domain (2026111332) found one call:
  when a case of an `Int64` activity column ends with a missing value,
  pandas counts the end activities with a NaN key, so the returned counts
  of `filter_df_on_end_activities_nocc` hold every present key as a float
  (`1.0`, not `1`). The fresh seed of the Polars CB domain (2026111331)
  was equal.
- **CC1-3 pandas sequence filters on more `datetime64` keys.** A new bank
  (`scripts/pandas_sequence_filter_cc_domain.py`: `datetime64` in s, ms
  and us around the epoch, us in Asia/Kolkata, ns in America/New_York
  across the DST change, object columns of naive Timestamps, Timestamps
  mixed with strings and `None`, and aware Timestamps of two zones; the
  activity arguments as Python datetimes in half of the cases) found:
  Python's messages name the types `datetime.datetime` and
  `datetime.date`; when pandas infers the dtype of a copied object column
  of Timestamps, those of one named zone become a column of that zone
  across its offsets, while two zones stay objects (the capture now sends
  the zone of an object column's Timestamps as `date_timezone`); on a
  `datetime64` column `isin` converts the boundary list
  only when it holds datetimes of the column's awareness (aware ones of
  one UTC offset) and `None` or NaN, and then matches by instant (a NaT
  boundary matches a list with `None` or NaN); any other list compares
  the Timestamps with the list's objects as Python does (NaT matches
  nothing; an aware Timestamp whose wall clock repeats in its zone equals
  no datetime of another `tzinfo`); the activity split matches a datetime
  argument against a naive s, ms or us activity by wall clock and an aware
  one by instant (not in a repeated hour), while a naive ns activity and a
  date argument match nothing.
- **CC1-4 Polars sequence filters with temporal and narrow numeric
  arguments.** A new bank (`scripts/polars_sequence_filter_cc_domain.py`:
  `Datetime` in ms, us Kolkata, ns New York and us Berlin across both 2021
  changes, around the epoch, `Date` around the epoch, `Int8` to `UInt64`
  and `Float32` with nulls; the arguments as Python datetimes, dates,
  ints, floats, bools or nested lists) found: Polars builds an argument
  list as `pl.lit` does (the items up to the first `None`; a list whose
  last item is a bool, int, float or str goes through the constructor of
  its first item, an int list taking bools and a float list ints and
  bools; any other list folds the supertype of its types in order,
  `failed to determine supertype of datetime[μs, UTC] and datetime[μs]`
  for naive and aware datetimes, and builds it strictly, `unexpected value
  while building Series of type Datetime('μs'); found value of type Date:
  2021-01-02` with its hint; an aware
  datetime with a fixed offset becomes UTC, one with a named zone keeps
  it); a prefix or suffix list compares with the activities when the two
  element types have a supertype and is then cast to the column dtype in
  the plan, otherwise the filter fails when it runs with `could not
  evaluate comparison between series 'activities' of dtype:
  List(Datetime('μs', 'Asia/Kolkata')) and series 'literal' of dtype:
  List(Datetime('μs', 'UTC'))`, the expression and the
  larger expression (`a | a` printed once, an empty pattern matching every
  case); datetime values cast to integer, float, `Date` and `Datetime`
  columns by their microseconds (days for `Date`, the column's unit for
  `Datetime`), and the plans print cast values in the column's dtype
  (floats as Polars prints them, datetimes in the column's zone with its
  abbreviation, fractions in 3, 6 or 9 digits); `ends_with` compares
  datetime suffix items as their String cast; the activity split implodes
  a scalar argument (`[2021-03-21 00:00:00.001 UTC.implode()]`) and builds it
  before it looks up the column.

Open (handed to round CD): a new domain for the Polars table filters
(`scripts/polars_filter_cc_domain.py`, with `--domain` and `--repeats` in
`scripts/capture-polars-filter-bank.py`: typed case columns and

included (the MSVC abbreviation masking of CC1-1 holds). It re-reviewed

  the sequence and table filters, which now also models `col(x) OP v`
  for a column dtype and a Python scalar as Polars 1.44 types it (probed
  per dtype, literal kind and operator): a str with a temporal side fails
  while the plan resolves (`cannot compare 'date/datetime/time' to a
  string value`); a number on a String column, any non-str on a
  Categorical or Enum column, a datetime on a small integer column, a
  datetime of another zone or awareness on a `Datetime` column and a bool
  on a temporal column fail when the filter runs, with the failing
  expression; a list fails on any column but a String one. A typed
  comparison prints coerced (`col("x") == 1`, `col("x").cast(Float64) ==
  1.5`, a constant `when(...).then(false).otherwise(null)` for an int out
  of the column's range, `null.repeat([col("x").len()])` for None,
  `is_between([lo, lo + 999 ns])` for `==` on a nanosecond column).
  Matching follows Polars: NaN equals NaN and sorts last, `Float32`
  compares in single precision, a microsecond literal is truncated on a
  millisecond column, Enum order is the category order.
- **CD1-2 Typed keys in the attribute, case, path and variant filters.**
  `Float32` case and activity columns are grouped and sorted; the numeric
  and value filters type their literals with CD1-1 on every column dtype;
  several `>=`, `<=` and `==` filters on one column merge into an
  interval in filter order as Polars' predicate pushdown merges them (a
  tighter bound replaces the current one, an equality bounds both sides,
  a literal without order against the bound is kept, dynamic literals and
  cast columns stay apart, an empty interval empties the frame, a point
  becomes `==`; only when the merge leaves fewer predicates); the
  statistics filters read the column's own values.
- **CD1-3 LTL plan resolution.** The whole plan resolves before a filter
  runs, so resolution errors come first, left inputs first: in
  `four_eyes_principle` activity 0 is the left input of pair 0 and a later
  activity first appears as the right input of pair (0, at);
  `eventually_follows` evaluates index 0, then n-1 down to 1. The plans
  print each activity comparison coerced (CD1-1), a missing value as
  `col(x) == null`, and `A_next_B_next_C`'s Python-side matching never
  equals a `datetime.date` with a `datetime.datetime`.
- **CD1-4 between.** A str anchor is wrapped in a list, a list (a dict:
  its keys) is a list literal built as `pl.lit` builds it (its strict
  rebuild and supertype errors), any other scalar is imploded by Polars.
  The second anchor resolves first and fails first, the type check before
  the Enum conversion; an imploded scalar names its element type
  `Unknown(Int(1))` or `Unknown(Float)`, prints `[x.implode()]` while it
  fails and `[x]` before it resolves, and once resolved casts to the
  column's list type (`[[1].cast(List(Int16))]`; a number that does not
  fit casts the column to its supertype, a float on integer data with
  `strict_cast(Float64)`). A datetime anchor on a `Date` column and any
  datetime on a millisecond column are refused as in CC1-4; a float
  anchor on a `Float32` column is rounded to single precision before the
  lookup (a float list is not). A temporal case id casts to String with
  its unit's fractional digits, and a result without a categorical column
  carries no categorical dtypes.
- **CD1-5 `filter_traces_attribute_in_timeframe` on typed attributes.**
  The attribute comparison follows CD1-1: resolution errors with the
  attribute filter's plan (an aware value printed in UTC), compute errors
  with the expression and the larger predicate, whose attribute part is
  printed coerced (a folded `when` with a leading dot); a list value
  fails on non-String columns; `pl.col` of a list with a non-str item
  raises `'int' object is not an instance of 'str'`.
- **CD1-6 variants join height.** A null case whose variant is in the
  list counts toward the join's list height (which decides between the
  list's order and the frame's), though its key never joins.
- **CD1-7 Fresh seeds of the typed domain.** Seeds 4243 and 4244 (and
  4245 of the base domain) found: an evaluated predicate of the attribute
  filters prints a folded comparison bare (`col("x").is_between([...])`,
  a `when` with a leading dot), as CD1-5 does; `filter_case_performance`
  with a None bound prints its null column after the other bound
  (`[(...) <= ([])]) & (null.repeat([col("case_duration").len()]))`); a
  datetime value of the attribute value filters on a `Datetime` column
  is looked up by its microseconds whatever the zones, as `is_in` looks
  it up (a UTC value finds a Kolkata cell of the same instant).
- **CD1-8 Re-review of CC.** A fresh seed of the Polars CC sequence domain
  (2026111342) was equal; a fresh seed of the pandas CC domain
  (2026111341) found one `rework.apply` call whose KeyError lists the two
  missing keys in Python's set order (declared in CC: hash seeds 3 and 4
  give the native order).
- **CD1-9 Full suite findings.** The first full ctest of the round failed
  six tests, fixed before the commit:
  - `minera_portable_integers`: the comparison model used `__int128`,
    which MSVC lacks. It now uses a portable signed 128-bit pair
    (`Wide`, exact products and sums, checked against `__int128` on 2
    million random operands) and an Int64-only range check.
  - Polars accepts any list in `is_in` on a `Null` column (int, float,
    str, bool, date, datetime lists all give 0 rows in 1.44.1); the shared
    `check_is_in` refused it (between and attribute vectors of round C1).
  - A Python int above the Int64 range is a UInt64 literal in Polars,
    which the model's signed values could not hold (vector B1-574). The
    attribute filters give it its own path, as 1.44.1 prints and
    evaluates it: `col("a") >= 9223372036854775809` on UInt64, Boolean
    cast to UInt64, signed integers cast to Float64 (`>= 9.2234e18`), a
    narrower unsigned column folded to a constant, temporal columns a
    `dyn int` that matches nothing, String and Categorical columns a
    ComputeError naming u64.
  - between keeps an empty categorical entry per column after it casts a
    categorical case id to String, as the frozen C1 vectors expect; the
    bank test reads that as the frame without categorical dtypes that the
    capture writes.

Declarations:

- The between result joins its segments back without an order: 14 of
  180 sampled calls gave another case order over six runs (case kinds
  str, int, Categorical, `Float32`, `UInt32`, `Datetime`), each case's
  rows staying in event order. `attr_value_different_persons` rarely does
  too (1 of 200 calls; seed 4243 case 201 gave cases [1, 2] in 7 of 16
  runs and [2, 1] in 9). The bank test compares both up to the case order
  when the captured order differs.
- `filter_on_ncases` keeps the first cases of a group_by without
  `maintain_order` on every case dtype (an `Int64` case column kept cases
  {4, 2, 1} in 7 of 12 runs and {4, 3, 1} in 5); the bank test accepts
  any equal-sized selection, as it did for Categorical columns.
- `filter_df_relative_occurrence_event_attribute` and
  `filter_df_keeping_activ_exc_thresh` print the `is_in` list of a
  group_by in its unspecified order; the bank test compares that list as
  a set.

Open (handed to round CE; banks and probes in the harness): six calls of
the fresh seeds. In the base domain (seed 4245, cases 357 and 757) Polars
moves bounds it merged after the unmerged predicates of the column,
left-nested (`(((x <= 50) & (x >= 7)) & (x >= "c")) & (x <= "d")`), and
prints a None bound's null column last in a left-nested chain; the native
plan keeps the merged bounds at the first position, right-nested. In the
typed domain (seed 4244): the stream filter predicates of two columns
come in another order when one of them fails (case 570, `org:resource ==
0` reported before `concept:name == "b"` on a `Float32` column);
`attr_value_different_persons` with an empty tuple on a `Datetime`
column fails in the reference (`could not evaluate comparison ... List(Null)`,
case 121) and not natively; and `filter_df_keeping_spno_activities`
ties at the cut (cases 804 and 1005) reach an error message, which lists
the kept activities, so the declared tie order shows in the text.
