## Review CE1: re-review of round CD, and edge values on typed keys in the Polars table filters (2026-11-14)

Round CE checked CD's CI run (43532993607) and fixed the six calls CD
left open, then extended the typed table filter domain with edge values.
Findings, all fixed:

- **CE1-1 CD's CI run on Windows.** Linux, macOS, the Python script
  tests, the frontend and the verifier were green; the Windows ctest
  failed in `minera_polars_filter_cc_bank_parity_tests` with 45 calls
  (`filter_df_relative_occurrence_event_attribute` 27,
  `filter_df_keeping_spno_activities` 11,
  `filter_df_keeping_activ_exc_thresh` 7), all on Europe/Berlin
  `Datetime` activity columns whose error text lists the kept values:
  MSVC's zone database names the zone "GMT+1" (ICU) where Polars prints
  "CET". The table filter bank test now masks the word after a wall time
  in error messages on MSVC only, as the sequence filter bank test does
  (CC1-1, declared in AY2).
- **CE1-2 CD1's open calls.** Predicate pushdown, modelled on 12,000
  random filter chains in Polars 1.44.1: walking down the plan, a filter
  joins the pending predicates under its column; one equal to a pending
  predicate is dropped, any other is combined in front (lower filters to
  the left); a filter on a null column stays where it is and the pending
  predicates join it. A node folds its columns left to right in bytewise
  order, the null filter right after the predicates of its own column.
  The interval merge runs on a node's whole conjunction and only when it
  leaves fewer comparisons: the node becomes the comparisons it did not
  merge, in order, then each column's lower and upper bound, folded to
  the left; an empty interval empties the frame below the lowest filter,
  and the filters above still run (and raise) on the empty frame. This
  fixes merged bounds and None bounds in the evaluated predicate (seed
  4245, cases 357 and 757) and the order of stream filters on two columns
  when one fails (seed 4244, case 570). LTL casts a list literal to
  String only on a String column; temporal, Boolean, Categorical and Enum
  columns compare it as a list and fail (`attr_value_different_persons`
  with an empty tuple on a `Datetime` column, case 121). The bank test
  checks `filter_df_keeping_spno_activities` ties as a tie set: a kept
  table holds k groups that no unkept group outranks (the null group may
  take a place but never keeps rows), and an error text lists every value
  all captured runs listed and only values some run listed (cases 804 and
  1005).
- **CE1-3 Edge values on typed keys.** `scripts/polars_filter_ce_domain.py`
  adds Boolean and `Null` activity columns, edge arguments (ints past
  2**53, at and past the Int64 range up to 2**64 - 1, ints that do not fit
  narrow columns, floats past 1e16, NaN, the infinities, -0.0, datetimes
  before 1970, bools, unknown strs, alone or in lists and tuples) and
  numeric filters on the activity column. Its first bank (seed
  2026111436) differed in 159 of 23,212 calls; CE1-4 to CE1-9 fixed them.
- **CE1-4 Python ints past the Int64 range.** The shared literal model
  holds them (decimal text up to 2**64 - 1): a scalar is an Int128 value,
  a list of non-negative ints and bools is UInt64 and any other such list
  builds strictly from its first item. Supertypes: Int128 takes Int64,
  Boolean and UInt64; UInt64 with Boolean stays UInt64; UInt64 with Int64,
  and either wide type with Float64, gives Float64. Comparisons follow
  CD1-9 in every table filter (they wrapped in the signed model outside
  the attribute filters). `is_in` with a UInt64 list casts signed columns
  to Int128 and narrower unsigned ones to UInt64, with an Int128 list
  every integer column to Int128; float columns read the values as
  floats; other dtypes fail (`'is_in' cannot check for List(UInt64)
  values in String data`).
- **CE1-5 Null and Boolean columns.** On a `Null` column a comparison
  casts the column to the literal's type (str, bool,
  `Datetime('μs'[, zone])`) while a dynamic int or float stays as written;
  `is_in` casts it to the element type (none for a null list), `==` with
  a list to `List(T)`, and a list of lists fails. A Boolean column
  compared with an int casts to `Int32` (`Int64` past its range).
- **CE1-6 List literals everywhere.** The LTL, timestamp, between, case
  and path filters build list arguments through the shared model, as the
  attribute filters do: construction TypeErrors, element types (naive
  datetimes as `Datetime('μs')`, the supertype fold) and the plan display,
  whose floats print as a frame prints them (`1e6`, `9.99999e5`,
  `1.0000e17`, `9.0072e15`, `0.3`). A datetime separator in between
  casts to String as Polars casts it (`2021-03-01 08:00:00.000000`).
- **CE1-7 Merge and comparison details.** Only comparisons on the bare
  column merge (a cast operand never does: Boolean, integer and temporal
  columns probed); literals of different classes are unordered and keep
  the first bound; a str on an Enum column merges as text whether or not
  it is a category. A microsecond literal reaches a millisecond column by
  floor division, so datetimes before 1970 round down.
- **CE1-8 Resolution errors.** A failing node prints the leaves before the
  failing one coerced (a None leaf as `null.repeat`) and those after it
  as written (`col > null`, `dyn int: 2`). A scalar `is_in` that resolves
  prints the scalar imploded and cast to the supertype of column and
  value (`col("x").cast(Int16).is_in([[300].cast(List(Int16))])` on
  `Int8`; `strict_cast(Int64)` for a negative value on `UInt64`;
  `strict_cast(Float64)` for a float on integers; a `Null` column cast to
  `Unknown(Int(v))`, `Unknown(Float)`, `Boolean` or the datetime type).
- **CE1-9 paths.** A list or tuple activity refuses the separator with
  Python's own TypeError (`can only concatenate list (not "str") to
  list`). In `apply_performance` a None bound after the failing bound
  drops from the larger expression (`[(failing) & (path test)]`); before
  it, the path test folds into `null.repeat([col("@@duration").len()])`.
- **CE1-10 Fresh seeds.** Seed 2026111437 found five calls (a resolved
  scalar `is_in` plan, a `Null` column with an empty-list stream value,
  `List(List(Null))` on a `Null` column, the paths None bound of CE1-9,
  and a declared row order below); seed 4246 found three (two Enum merges
  of a category and a non-category str, a `Null` column with a UInt64
  list). Seed 4247 found three: an `==` on a nanosecond column, which
  Polars prints as `is_between([v, v + 999 ns])`, merges with other
  bounds as the range it is (lower `v`, upper `v + 999 ns`); between's
  separator error casts a case column of any dtype but String with
  `strict_cast(String)` and prints the anchors resolved
  (`is_in([[1].cast(List(Float32))])`, in the `_first_act` and
  `_last_act` filters too); and a declared case order below. All fixed.

Declarations:

- `filter_traces_intersecting` keeps the cases of a group_by in an
  unspecified order: seed 2026111437 case 518 captured one order in all
  six runs, while 16 reruns over hash seeds 0-3 gave both. The bank in
  the suite does not hit it.
- `filter_on_case_performance` keeps its cases in an unspecified order as
  well: seed 4247 case 333 captured one order, while 18 reruns over hash
  seeds 0-2 gave both.

Not covered: Duration, Time, Decimal and Int128 columns (no table cell
for their values) and ints above the UInt64 range (not in the bank's
typed JSON).

## Review CF1: re-review of round CE, and scalar values, odd bounds and argument shapes in the Polars table filters (2026-11-14)

Round CF checked CE's CI run (43543514400: green on all six jobs, the
Windows ctest 488/488 with the abbreviation mask), replayed fresh seeds of
the CE domain, and added a domain for the argument shapes the earlier
banks left out. Findings, all fixed or declared:

- **CF1-1 Fresh CE seeds.** Seeds 2026111450, 4250 and 4251 (17,425,
  17,382 and 17,432 calls on 600 frames) differed in 0, 1 and 1 calls: a
  list value of `filter_traces_attribute_in_timeframe` on a Categorical
  column with an empty time window (CF1-6), and a case order of
  `filter_on_case_performance` (seed 4251 case 94, declared below).
- **CF1-2 New domain.** `scripts/polars_filter_cf_domain.py` (on top of
  the CE domain) adds per case `attributes.apply`, `apply_events` and
  `filter_df_on_attribute_values` with scalar values (None, typed and
  edge values, a missing case key), `apply_numeric(_events)` on any column
  with odd and typed bounds and up to two stream filters, `between.apply`
  with typed, edge, None, empty, nested and tuple anchors on other
  columns, edge bounds of the timestamp filters and
  `filter_traces_attribute_in_timeframe` with typed, list, all-str list,
  tuple, dict and None values, and the paths filters with odd path shapes
  (3-tuples, lists, the str "ab") and odd bounds. Its first bank (seed
  2026111460) differed in 85 of 30,328 calls; CF1-3 to CF1-8 fixed them.
- **CF1-3 Float display.** Polars prints a `dyn float` literal with
  Rust's Display (the shortest digits, never an exponent: 2**63 as
  `9223372036854776000`, 1e17 as `100000000000000000`), and a Float64
  literal or frame cell with its `fmt_float`: an integral value under
  999999 with one decimal; a Rust display longer than nine characters in
  scientific notation with four decimals outside [1e-6, 999999] and
  rounded to six decimals inside; any other integral value in the
  shortest scientific notation (`1e7`, `9.99999e5`, `1.234567e6`); the
  rest as Rust prints them. The plan display used sampled thresholds and
  printed 1e7 as `1.0000e7` (in the paths and case performance bounds);
  plans and frames now share one function, checked on 36 probed values
  and on 2,000,000 random doubles against the CE frame model.
- **CF1-4 Scalar values in the attribute filters.** A None value folds a
  positive membership to `false.alias(key)`, as an empty list does (the
  trace filters always use the positive plan). A negative int or a
  datetime before 1970 meets a UInt64 column in Int64, so cells past the
  Int64 range turn null and match nothing. A datetime on a Datetime
  column and a date on a Date column resolve their scalar `is_in` without
  a cast.
- **CF1-5 Lists on Null columns and list merges.** A Null column cannot
  order a list: `>=`, `>`, `<=` and `<` raise `InvalidOperationError:
  cannot perform '>=' comparison between series 'x' of dtype: list[i64]
  and series 'literal' of dtype: list[i64]`, naming physical types
  (dates `i32`, datetimes `i64`, nested lists nested), while `==` and
  `!=` compare and match nothing. In the interval merge list literals
  compare only as equal or not at all: equal lists merge into `==`,
  others (`[1]` and `[3]`, `[1]` and `[1.0]`) stay and never fold to an
  empty frame. The model compared their display text, so
  `rd >= [1969-12-31 23:59:59.999]` and `rd <= [""]` emptied the frame
  where Polars raised the stream filter's error (case 212). In
  `between.apply` a Null activity column casts to the type of a resolved
  scalar anchor (`cast(Boolean)`, `Int32` for a dynamic int, `Int64` past
  it, `UInt64` past the Int64 range, `Float64`, the datetime or `Date`
  type; None stays `[[null]]`).
- **CF1-6 filter_traces_attribute_in_timeframe.** Only a String column
  refuses a list value while the plan resolves; Categorical and Enum
  columns compare it while collecting, which an empty time window skips,
  and a Null column casts to the list's type
  (`col("x").cast(List(String)) == ["r1"]`) and keeps no row. An
  attribute on the timestamp column itself is filtered apart from the
  window: its errors name no larger expression, and an empty window does
  not skip them. A dict value is a struct literal; on a String column
  Polars compares the cell with the struct's String cast (`"{"z","x"}"`,
  `"}"` for an empty dict, `null` when a field is None), now modelled for
  str, int and bool fields in the plan and the match.
- **CF1-7 paths.** List bounds go through the shared literal model
  (`[(col("@@duration")) <= ([9.0072e15, -1.5])]`, `List(Float64)`); an
  int past the Int64 range is a UInt64 literal that meets the Int64
  duration at Float64 (`col("@@duration").cast(Float64) >= 9.2234e18`,
  in `filter_on_case_performance` too); equal str or list bounds merge
  into one `==` (`could not evaluate comparison ...` without the
  operator).
- **CF1-8 filter_on_ncases.** pm4py keeps the first k ids of an unordered
  `unique`; a null id among them keeps no rows, so a frame with a null
  case id keeps k or k - 1 cases (seed 2026111460 case 346 kept {2}, {3}
  or {2, 3} of {null, 2, 3} over 24 runs). The bank test accepts the
  frame's rows of any k ids, or k - 1 when the frame has a null id.
- **CF1-9 Fresh CF seeds.** Seeds 2026111461 and 4261 (26,585 and 26,543
  calls on 700 frames) differed in 1 and 0 calls: equal list bounds in
  paths (CF1-7, seed 2026111461 case 519). Seed 4262 (26,781 calls on
  700 frames) found two: a NaN lower bound above a lower upper bound,
  which Polars' interval merge orders totally (NaN above every number and
  equal to itself) and so folds to an empty frame (case 448: the model
  left NaN unordered and raised the stream filter's error), and a case
  order of `filter_case_performance` (case 27, both orders over 18
  reference runs; compared as case blocks). CE seed 4263 (17,473 calls on
  600 frames) found one: equal empty-list bounds of
  `filter_case_performance` merge into one `==`, the whole predicate
  (case 400). All fixed.

Declarations:

- Polars 1.44.1 panics (a pyo3 `PanicException`: "implementation error,
  cannot get ref Int32 from Int64") in `between.apply` on a Null activity
  column with the Int64 anchors 0 and -2**63. The domain records the
  panic and the bank test does not compare it.
- Datetime arguments outside the nanosecond range (before 1677-09-21 or
  after 2262-04-11) are refused by the shared literal model instead of
  wrapping.
- Dict values of `filter_traces_attribute_in_timeframe` beyond CF1-6 are
  refused (`Native Polars timeframe filters take dict (struct) attribute
  values on String columns with str, int and bool fields only`) and the
  bank test counts the refusal as declared (46 of the CF bank's 74 dict
  calls). Probed: a numeric column casts to a one-field struct of the
  field's type (zero or several fields raise `must specify one field in
  the struct`), Boolean, Date and Datetime columns raise a SchemaError
  naming `Struct({...})`, Categorical and Enum columns a ComputeError
  (`cannot compare categorical with struct[N]`), a Null column keeps no
  row; all of these are collect-time errors that an empty window skips.
- `filter_on_case_performance` and `filter_case_performance` keep cases
  in an unspecified order (seed 4251 case 94 and seed 4262 case 27, as
  CE's seed 4247 case 333) and are compared as case blocks.

Not reachable: `validate_bound` with several paths (a CE target), since
`paths.apply_performance` takes exactly one path (a list of paths raises
a TypeError before any bound is read); `apply_numeric` reads only
`stream_filter_key1` and `stream_filter_key2`, so a node holds at most
three columns.

## Review CG1: re-review of round CF, and dict values on every column, list and str bounds of the case filters and predicate order in the Polars table filters (2026-11-14)

Round CG checked CF's CI run (43553607248: green on all six jobs, the
CF bank on Windows for the first time), replayed fresh seeds of the CF
and CE domains, modelled the dict values CF refused, and added a domain
for them and for the case filters' bounds. Findings, all fixed:

- **CG1-1 Fresh CF and CE seeds.** CF seeds 2026111470 and 4270 (26,559
  and 26,502 calls on 700 frames) and CE seeds 2026111471 and 4271
  (17,432 and 17,450 calls on 600 frames) differed in 3, 2, 2 and 1
  calls. A list value of `filter_traces_attribute_in_timeframe` that a
  typed column refuses while resolving prints in the failed plan as the
  literal model shows it (`col("act") == [2020-12-31 18:30:00 UTC]`, a
  tuple of a float and an int as `[10.0, 1.0]`), not as the transported
  text (CF 2026111470 cases 99 and 414, CF 4270 case 6). A failing str
  lower bound of `filter_case_performance` with a None upper bound names
  no larger expression (CE 2026111471 case 145, CF 4270 case 197; CG1-5).
  Inverted str bounds of `paths.apply_performance` (min `"b"`, max `""`)
  fold to an empty interval instead of raising (CF 2026111470 case 394;
  CG1-5). The one-item path `[65536]` raises pm4py's `unsupported operand
  type(s) for +: 'int' and 'str'`: the first item meets the separator
  before the second is read (CE 4271 case 528; the model read both first
  and raised an IndexError). `filter_df_keeping_spno_activities` keeps
  any k of tied activities, null among them (CE 2026111471 case 516: the
  `is_in` list held null in the reference run and another tied value in
  the native one); the bank test now accepts a listing of the captured
  form and size that is a valid top-k selection of the frame's counts.
- **CG1-2 New domain.** `scripts/polars_filter_cg_domain.py` (on top of
  the CF domain) builds the CF frames, sometimes with a copy `zz` of
  another column so that the attribute sorts after the timestamp column,
  and gives each case `filter_traces_attribute_in_timeframe` with dicts of
  none, one or two fields (a repeated key, None, typed, edge and str
  fields) on every column, mostly over a window that holds every event,
  sometimes an empty, inverted or random one;
  `filter_case_performance`, `filter_on_case_performance` and
  `filter_on_case_size` with list (typed, nested, empty, None items, wide
  ints), str (inverted or equal pairs), None and odd numeric bounds; and
  `paths.apply_performance` with str bound pairs and one-item paths. Its
  first bank (seed 2026111480, 1,000 frames, 6,294 calls, written
  alongside CG1-3 and CG1-5) differed in 3 calls (CG1-4).
- **CG1-3 Dict values on every column.** A dict is a struct literal
  whose fields take the types `pl.lit` gives the Python values (a
  repeated key keeps its first place and its last value). Probed on 19
  column dtypes with 36 dicts each (684 probes, `sp.py`): a String column
  compares with the struct's String cast (CF1-6). An integer or float
  column casts to a struct of each field's supertype with the column
  (a str field `String`; a Float64 column `Float64`; a Float32 column
  `Float32` for None, bool and date fields, else `Float64`; on integer
  columns None and bool fields keep the column's type, a float field
  `Float64`, an int field `Int64` (`Float64` on `UInt64`), an int past
  the Int64 range `Int128`, a datetime field `Int64` and a date field
  `Int32` or `Int64` on 32- and 64-bit columns only) and prints the
  struct in those types: `col("x").cast(Struct({'a': Int64, 'b':
  Float64})) == {1609459200000000,1.0}`. A struct of one field compares
  that field; none or several raise `InvalidOperationError: must specify
  one field in the struct` (naming the cast) while collecting, and only
  when the column holds a valid cell, since an empty or all-null column
  casts. A field without a supertype (a datetime on `Int8`) leaves the
  column uncast: `SchemaError: could not evaluate comparison between
  series 'x' of dtype: i8 and series 'literal' of dtype: Struct({...})`.
  A Null column casts to the literal's struct and keeps no row; Boolean,
  Date and Datetime columns raise that SchemaError, Categorical and Enum
  columns `ComputeError: cannot compare categorical with struct[N]`.
  Nested field values stay refused (no probe). CF's refusal and its
  declaration in the bank test are gone.
- **CG1-4 Predicate order.** Polars pushes the attribute filter and the
  window down as one predicate whose parts follow the byte order of their
  column names, so an attribute column after the timestamp column (`zz`)
  comes second in the larger expression. An equal window merges into one
  `==` leaf, which the merge places after the unmerged parts: the
  attribute then comes second only when it merges too, as a bare column
  against a typed literal (not a cast column, a `dyn` literal, a folded
  constant or a null column; probed per form, `ord4.py` to `ord6.py`).
  The CG bank's three calls (cases 101, 275 and 692) had the window first.
- **CG1-5 Case filter bounds.** A list bound names its `pl.lit` type in
  the SchemaError (`List(Int64)`, `List(String)`, `List(UInt64)` past the
  Int64 range, `List(List(Int64))`, `List(Null)`, `List(Float64)` for
  `[1.5, None]`) and prints as the literal model shows it; the other bound
  prints as Polars coerces it against the `UInt32` count or the `Int64`
  duration (a float casts the column, a wide int meets it at Float64, a
  bool folds). `filter_on_case_size` reports the larger expression and
  merges equal str or list bounds into one `==` as the performance
  filters do. A None upper bound leaves a failing lower bound alone (no
  larger expression); a None lower bound folds to a null column printed
  after the failing upper bound. A str lower bound above a str upper
  bound (byte order) folds the interval to an empty one in all three case
  filters and in `paths.apply_performance`: nothing raises and no case or
  path passes (probed with `cl.py`, `cl2.py`, `cl3.py`, `cp.py` and
  `sb.py`).
- **CG1-6 Fresh CG seeds.** Seeds 4280 and 2026111481 (6,324 calls on
  1,000 frames each) differed in 2 and 0 calls: a dict with one None
  field on an all-null `Float64` or `UInt16` column (seed 4280 cases 549
  and 557). Polars casts an all-null column to null structs, which match
  nothing, and any other column to valid structs with a null field, so a
  null cell matches a None field only when the column holds a valid cell
  (`sn.py`); the model matched it always. Seed 4281 (6,332 calls on
  1,000 frames) differed in 0.

Not taken (carried to CH): Polars casts a float to String with its own
display (`1e-5` as `0.00001`, `1e-7` as `1e-7`), which the struct String
cast of a float field and the `string_cast` of Float32 cells follow only
where Python's `repr` agrees; nested dict fields.

## Review CH1: re-review of round CG, and Polars' Float to String cast, nested dict fields and odd float activities in the Polars filters (2026-11-14)

Round CH checked CG's CI run (43562859480: green on all six jobs, the
CG bank on Windows for the first time), replayed fresh seeds of the CG,
CF and CE domains, modelled Polars' own cast of a float to String and the
nested dict fields CG refused, and added two domains of odd float
activities (one for the table filters, one for the sequence filters).
Findings, all fixed:

- **CH1-1 Fresh CG, CF and CE seeds.** CG seeds 2026111490 and 4290
  (6,390 and 6,333 calls on 1,000 frames), CF seed 2026111491 (26,639
  calls on 700 frames) and CE seed 2026111492 (17,420 calls on 600
  frames) differed in 0, 1, 1 and 0 calls, both reference-random:
  `filter_on_case_size` (CG 4290 case 530) and
  `filter_df_on_attribute_values` (CF 2026111491 case 366) keep their
  cases in either order (both orders about evenly over 80 runs and four
  hash seeds). The bank test accepts any case order for them, as it does
  for `filter_on_case_performance`.
- **CH1-2 Polars' Float to String cast.** Polars casts a float to String
  with its own display, not Python's `repr`: the shortest digits that read
  back (as a float for a Float32 column) in fixed notation while the
  leading digit's decimal exponent is below 16 (Float32: 13) and at least
  -5 (Float32: -6), integral values ending in `.0`, other values as
  `d.ddde+X` or `d.ddde-X` without padding (`1e-5` casts to `"0.00001"`,
  `1e-7` to `"1e-7"`, `1e16` to `"1e+16"`, `0.1` on Float32 to `"0.1"`).
  `polars_cast_float` (fitted on 805,046 Float64 and Float32 values
  against Polars 1.44.1 without a difference) replaces the `repr` in
  `string_cast`, in the struct String cast of float fields and in the
  String casts of the between, paths and variants filters (case ids,
  path labels, variant strings). A dynamic float literal casts as a
  Float64 does (9,024 values), so a float suffix of `ends_with` reads
  `0.00001` too.
- **CH1-3 Nested dict fields.** A dict field of a timeframe dict value is
  a nested struct whose fields cast recursively to their supertypes with
  the column (`Struct({'j': Struct({'a': Float64})})`); a String column
  compares with the nested String cast (`{{1.0}}`). On an integer or float
  column a struct of one nested field raises `InvalidOperationError:
  Cannot cast from struct to other types` while collecting, and only when
  the column holds a present cell. A list field never casts the column (a
  SchemaError on integer and float columns, the String cast on String
  columns, `{[1, 2]}`), and a list that `pl.lit` cannot build (mixed
  types, an int list meeting a float, a list after an int) raises
  `TypeError: cannot create expression literal for value of type dict`
  while pm4py builds the comparison, after the attribute column is
  selected and before the timestamp column is read (probed with 35 lists
  and 342 dict and column pairs). A repeated key keeps its first place
  and its last value, so an earlier value is never built. Lists of dicts
  stay refused (declared).
- **CH1-4 New table domain.** `scripts/polars_filter_ch_domain.py` (on
  top of the CG domain) gives activity and case columns odd floats
  (`1e-5`, `1e-7`, `1e16`, `0.1` on Float32, `-0.0`, `1/3`, NaN,
  infinities, subnormals, `1.7976931348623157e308`), sometimes adds a
  String column `zz` of struct texts (`{0.00001}`, `{[1, 2]}`, `{{1}}`,
  `}`), passes the column's floats as activity values and gives the
  timeframe filter dicts with odd float fields, the strs Polars casts them
  to, lists (nested, empty, with None) and nested dicts. Its first bank
  (seed 2026111495, 800 frames, 31,888 calls) differed in 174 calls:
  - a number meets a Float32 column cast to Float32 in the attribute
    filters (`1e-5` finds the cell `1e-5` rounded to Float32; the model
    compared it as a double);
  - a str value that names a column is that column in `is_in`
    (`col("concept:name").is_in(col("org:resource"))`): the two columns
    meet in their supertype (Float64 over integers; Float32 with integers
    of up to 16 bits; the wider of two same-signed integers; a signed and
    an unsigned integer in a signed type twice as wide, Int128 with
    UInt64), an int column read as a float column prints
    `.strict_cast(Float64)`, a Null side casts to the other's type, and
    other pairs raise `'is_in' cannot check for List(Z) values in X data`
    (probed on a 19 by 19 dtype matrix);
  - two list values of the attribute filters merge when Polars finds them
    equal: `-0.0` equals `0.0` and two NaNs are equal inside lists;
  - the String casts of CH1-2 and the nested dicts of CH1-3;
  - 61 calls carried ints past the UInt64 range (`int(1e22)`,
    `int(1.7976931348623157e308)`) that the bank's typed JSON cannot
    carry; the domain now keeps such values as floats.
  The recaptured bank (31,894 calls) differed in 1 call:
  `filter_traces_contained` keeps its cases in either order (case 294,
  both orders over 60 runs and three hash seeds; accepted by the bank
  test).
- **CH1-5 New sequence domain.**
  `scripts/polars_sequence_filter_ch_domain.py` (on top of the CC
  sequence domain) gives the activity column the same odd floats and
  passes them (sometimes as ints or strs) as activity values. Its first
  bank (seed 2026111496, 1,500 frames, 19,761 calls) differed in 23
  calls:
  - `ends_with` casts a float suffix as Polars casts a Float64 to String
    (`0.00001`), which the variant string of a Float activity holds; the
    model used `repr` (`1e-05`);
  - `activity_split` with a scalar int or float passes a dynamic literal
    that takes a Float32 column's type (`0.1` matches the cell `0.1f`,
    `16777217` matches `16777216.0`), while a list is a Float64 Series
    that meets the column widened (`[0.1]` matches no `0.1f`);
  - `consecutive_act_case_grouping` returns its groups from a `group_by`
    without `maintain_order`, in another order on every run (both orders
    over 30 runs under each of four hash seeds); the bank test compares
    its rows unordered.
  Seed 2026111497 (900 frames, 11,301 calls) differed in 0.
- **CH1-6 Wide ints on Float32.** An int meets a Float32 column rounded
  to Float32 straight from its digits (`2**63 + 2**39 + 1` rounds up to
  `2**63 + 2**40`; through a double it would tie down to `2**63`), and an
  int past the Int64 range compares as its unsigned value; the between
  filter printed such an int as its signed bits
  (`[-1].cast(List(Float32))` for `18446744073709551615`). A probe domain
  of wide floats and ints on Float32 activities (seed 77, 150 frames,
  6,021 calls) differed in 90 calls before and 1 after (an
  `apply_numeric` case order, both orders over 20 runs; accepted by the
  bank test). The conversion halves an unsigned int past the Int64 range
  with a sticky bit, so it rounds the same on every compiler (checked
  against numpy on 200,001 values).
- **CH1-7 Fresh CH seeds.** Seed 4295 (800 frames, 32,068 calls)
  differed in 3 calls. Each NaN reaches Python as its own float object,
  so a variant tuple holding a NaN equals no other: two cases with NaN
  activities are two variants of `filter_variants_top_k` (`k=-1` then
  keeps one and fails joining it; the ties then compare `(nan,)` with
  `(None,)` and fail the sort); the model merged them (cases 65 and 149,
  probed with `vn.py`). `filter_df_relative_occurrence_event_attribute`
  with an empty key tuple and `KEEP_ONCE_PER_CASE` resolves the case key
  first (a missing one raises its ColumnNotFoundError before the tuple's
  IndexError; case 74). Seed 2026111498 (800 frames, 32,045 calls)
  differed in 1 call: a String attribute column read against an Enum
  column named by a str value is cast strictly to that Enum
  (`col("org:resource").strict_cast(Enum([...]))`), which fails while
  collecting on a str outside the categories (``conversion from `str` to
  `enum` failed in column 'org:resource' for 9 out of 9 values: ["r2",
  "r2", … "r2"]``, the larger expression ending in `.not()` for a
  negative event filter); an Enum column read against a String column
  casts the imploded column instead and names no column (case 108,
  probed with `en.py`).

Not taken (carried to CI): dicts and the comparison model on Duration,
Time, Decimal and Int128 columns (no table cell in the transport;
declared), lists of dicts as dict fields (declared), the remaining
`coerced_scalar_is_in` gaps (str and Categorical/Enum columns), `list_literal`
with wide ints after a float and in nested lists, `lit_supertype` of
Int128 with temporal types, ints past the UInt64 range as paths bounds,
`plan_text_at` when the failing leaf is inside a merged node, and the
items carried from CD.

## Review CI1: re-review of round CH, and dict and list-of-dict values in the Polars table filters (2026-11-14)

Round CI checked CH's CI run (43572000391: green on all six jobs, the CH
banks on Windows for the first time), replayed fresh seeds of the CH, CG,
CF and CE domains, checked the remaining float-as-text sites of the
Polars table filters, and added a domain that passes dicts, lists of
dicts and lists Polars cannot build to the attribute, LTL, paths and
timeframe filters. Findings, all fixed:

- **CI1-1 Fresh CH, CG, CF and CE seeds.** CH table seeds 2026111401 and
  4301 (31,999 and 32,003 calls on 800 frames), CH sequence seed
  2026111402 (11,796 calls on 900 frames), CG seed 2026111403 (6,344
  calls on 1,000 frames), CF seed 2026111404 (26,506 calls on 700 frames)
  and CE seed 2026111405 (17,421 calls on 600 frames) differed in 0 calls
  but one: `eventually_follows` keeps its cases in either order (CH 4301
  case 497, both orders over 18 runs and three hash seeds; the bank test
  now accepts any case order for it, as for `attr_value_different_persons`).
- **CI1-2 Struct literals in `pl.lit` lists.** A dict inside a list value
  (`[{"a": 0.1}, {"b": 1e16}]`) is a struct item of the list literal; the
  shared literal model (`src/backend/polars_lit_model.hpp`) now builds it
  as Polars 1.44.1 does (probed with about 500 lists):
  - the fields take the types `pl.lit` gives the Python values, a repeated
    key its first place and its last value;
  - two structs with the same field names in the same order take each
    field's supertype; other structs take the union of their fields in the
    longer one's order (the first one's on a tie), then the shorter one's
    new fields, a common field the supertype of the shorter one's type with
    the longer one's (so in `[{"r": {"a": 1.0}, "x": 1.0}, {"r": {"b":
    1.0}, "y": 1.0}]` the field `r` is `Struct({'b', 'a'})`); a struct and
    an int or float take the number into every field (failing if a field
    cannot take it, a list field always); a str turns a struct into String;
    a bool, date, datetime or list fails (`failed to determine supertype
    of bool and struct[1]`, `of struct[2] and struct[1]` for a failing
    field);
  - a strict struct build first fails on any value that is neither a struct
    nor None (`unexpected value while building Series of type
    Struct({'b': Float64}); found value of type Float64: 1.0000e17`); a
    struct without fields takes any value as `{}`; then each field builds
    strictly in field order, its errors naming the field in the context
    stack above `Series ''` (`[1] while constructing Series 'b'`, the
    innermost field first);
  - inside a nested list a struct casts to a struct by field name and a
    number to a struct of one plain field; other casts fail (`unexpected
    value while building Series of type List(Struct(...))`), and so does a
    struct with one field that fails to cast (an int field meeting a
    struct of two fields); a struct cast to String is its display
    (`{1,"y"}`);
  - the display prints fields in braces with the frame's float display
    (`{1.0000e16,0.0000001}`) and truncates long lists (`[{1}, {2}, …
    {4}]`).
- **CI1-3 `is_in` with struct items.** A list holding a dict fails `is_in`
  on every column dtype, Null included, without a cast in the plan:
  `'is_in' cannot check for Float64 values in List(Struct({'a':
  Float64})) data`. A dict value's keys are the operand (as before), a
  repeated key once in its first place.
- **CI1-4 Dicts in the LTL filters.** `eventually_follows`,
  `A_next_B_next_C`, `four_eyes_principle` and
  `attr_value_different_persons` compare a dict activity as the timeframe
  filter compares a dict (round CG's model, moved into the shared literal
  model): the String cast on String columns, the one-field cast on integer
  and float columns (`must specify one field in the struct` and `Cannot
  cast from struct to other types` only on a column with a present cell),
  SchemaErrors on the other columns and `cannot compare categorical with
  struct[1]` on Categorical and Enum columns, each with pm4py's
  expression and larger expression. A dict whose list field `pl.lit`
  cannot build raises pm4py's `cannot create expression literal for value
  of type dict` while the filter is built.
- **CI1-5 LTL filter order and missing columns.** `eventually_follows`
  runs its first activity's filter, then the last one's, then the others
  in order (probed with 3 to 5 activities; round CE's fit of "the others
  from the last one back" only held for three). `A_next_B_next_C` with a
  missing attribute column on an empty frame never reads the column: its
  empty selection fails the join (`datatypes of join keys don't match`).
- **CI1-6 Lists of dicts in the timeframe filter.** A list of dicts, as
  the value or as a dict field, is now built as a `List(Struct(...))`
  literal instead of refused: a list field never casts the column (a
  SchemaError on integer and float columns, the String cast on String
  columns), and a list that cannot be built raises pm4py's TypeError while
  the comparison is built.
- **CI1-7 Floats as text.** The CI domain passes floats whose Rust
  display, Python `repr`, `std::to_chars` and Polars' plan display differ
  (`1e16`, `1e-7`, `1e-5`, `1e22`, `5e-324`, `0.30000000000000004`,
  `9007199254740993.0`, `-0.0`) as scalars, list items and dict fields to
  every value of these filters; they print as Polars prints them. The
  `real_text` calls left in the attribute, case, LTL and timestamp filters
  are fallbacks for literals the reference never shows; the LTL and
  timestamp ones now print a dynamic float in Rust's display as the
  others do.
- **CI1-8 New table domain.** `scripts/polars_filter_ci_domain.py` (on top
  of the CH domain) adds dicts with odd float, nested dict and list
  fields, lists and tuples of dicts, lists Polars cannot build (an odd
  float next to a str, a list next to a float, a dict next to a scalar),
  nested float lists and odd floats to the attribute filters
  (`apply`, `apply_events`, `filter_df_on_attribute_values`), the four LTL
  filters, `paths.apply` and the timeframe filter, on the activity
  column, another column or a missing one. Its first bank (seed
  2026111410, 300 frames, 13,712 calls) differed in 641 calls (281
  timeframe, 202 attribute, 158 LTL): lists of dicts refused or built
  with the wrong type, error or field order, struct `is_in` failures,
  dict LTL activities, the `eventually_follows` order and the empty-frame
  join. After CI1-2 to CI1-6: 0. Seed 4402 (500 frames, 22,843 calls)
  differed in 0 calls on its first capture; seed 2026111412 (400 frames,
  18,384 calls) in 1 (case 354: a list field whose struct items meet an
  int field and a struct field of two fields under one name; the model
  nulled the failing field instead of failing the build), fixed; seed
  4403 (400 frames, 18,301 calls) in 0.

Not taken (carried to CJ): a list whose first item is a plain list and a

## Review CJ1: re-review of round CI, and dict values in the bounds, anchors and activities of the Polars table and sequence filters (2026-11-14)

Round CJ checked CI's CI run (43580317951: green on all six jobs),
replayed fresh seeds of the CI, CH, CG, CF and CE domains, and added two
domains: one passes dicts as the bounds and anchors of the numeric,
relative occurrence, between, case and paths performance filters, the
other dicts as the activity values of the sequence filters. Findings, all
fixed:

- **CJ1-1 Fresh CI, CH, CG, CF and CE seeds.** CI seed 2026111420 (18,277
  calls on 400 frames), CH table seed 2026111421 (32,007 calls on 800
  frames), CH sequence seed 2026111422 (11,601 calls on 900 frames), CG
  seed 2026111423 (6,314 calls on 1,000 frames), CF seed 2026111424
  (26,624 calls on 700 frames) and CE seed 2026111425 (17,422 calls on 600
  frames) differed in 0 calls but one: CE case 87, `between.apply` on a
  Null activity column. There the resolved `is_in` of a dynamic number
  keeps its unresolved type (`col("concept:name").cast(Unknown(Float))`,
  `.cast(Unknown(Int(1)))`, `.cast(Unknown(Int(18446744073709551615)))`),
  in the membership and the separator plans alike. Round CF's fit
  (`Float64`, `Int32`, `Int64`, `UInt64`) never met a bank case.
- **CJ1-2 Dicts through `pl.lit`.** A dict converts strictly, through
  Polars' own value conversion, while Python builds the expression. A list
  field that fails to build fails the whole literal with `cannot create
  expression literal for value of type dict` and the `allow_object=True`
  hint, whatever the list's own error. 8,000 random dicts agree with the
  model in acceptance and display. A struct cast to String is `}` without
  fields, null with a None field at its top level, else its display
  (`{1,"x"}`).
- **CJ1-3 Dict bounds of the case filters.** In `filter_case_performance`,
  `filter_on_case_performance` and `filter_on_case_size` a dict bound is a
  struct literal:
  - the UInt32 size or the Int64 duration is cast to a struct of each
    field's supertype with it; a list field leaves the column alone;
  - the bound then always fails. On a present cell the cast fails (`must
    specify one field in the struct` past one field, `Cannot cast from
    struct to other types` for a nested one). Without one, the struct
    comparison fails (`cannot perform '<=' comparison between series ...
    struct[1]`). A column left alone gives the SchemaError (`could not
    evaluate '<=' comparison`);
  - the failing node is the cast when the cast fails. The larger
    expression is the whole predicate, as for the other bounds;
  - equal dicts merge into one comparison unless the column is cast.

  With four threads the narrow aggregated duration frame can race to the
  comparison error instead of the cast error. The reference shows both
  messages across runs, so this is declared reference nondeterminism: the
  bank test accepts the comparison error where the model gives the cast
  error.
- **CJ1-4 Dicts in the paths filters.** `paths.apply_performance` treats
  dict bounds as the case performance bounds do, on the duration. The
  cast fails only when two rows of one case have timestamps. A dict whose
  list field cannot build raises the TypeError of CJ1-2. In `paths.apply`
  a dict path item never reaches Polars on any column: pm4py joins each
  path into a str first, so it fails with Python's own error
  (`unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'dict' and 'str'`, `can only
  concatenate str (not "dict") to str`). The CJ bank has about 300 such
  calls, and all of them match.
- **CJ1-5 Dicts in the numeric attribute filters.** In `apply_numeric` and
  `apply_numeric_events` dict bounds and stream filter values convert
  strictly (CJ1-2) and compare as structs: the String cast on String
  columns, the cast column on integer, float and Null columns.
  - On a String column a dict merges with the other bound as the str it
    casts to. On any other column it merges only with an equal dict, and
    only when the column is not cast (Boolean, temporal, a field without a
    supertype). Against any other literal the bound stays as it is
    (`m1.py`).
  - A dict that casts to a null str compares with that null (`[(col("x"))
    <= (null)]`) under an AND, and folds to `null.repeat(...)` under an OR
    (`q4.py`).
  - In a resolved plan, a dict after the failing leaf prints as written
    (`{null,false}`).
- **CJ1-6 Odd stakes of the relative occurrence filter.**
  `filter_df_relative_occurrence_event_attribute` with a dict, set or
  frozenset stake raises Python's `unsupported operand type(s) for *:
  'dict' and 'int'`.
- **CJ1-7 Lists that mix lists, lists of dicts and scalars.** A strictly
  built list type that meets an item holding structs
  (`pl.lit([[1], [{"a": 1}], 5])`) casts the item to its element type
  field by field. A String element takes the struct's String cast. A
  struct that casts keeps its struct type and fails in the list builder at
  once (`cannot build list with different dtypes`), before items that
  failed their cast are reported. A struct cast to a non-struct type
  raises when one of its fields does (`l3.py`).
- **CJ1-8 Dict activity values in the sequence filters.**
  - `activity_split` uses a dict's unique keys as the activities.
  - The value calls dedupe dict keys by type and text.
  - `ends_with` builds every item's literal first (a list's or a dict's
    TypeError), and the String casts fail after that. A dict item is the
    suffix of its String cast.
  - In `prefixes` and `suffixes`, a pattern of structs on an integer or
    float column whose type every leaf meets is cast to the column dtype,
    field by field. A single plain field compares as its value; the plan
    shows the struct with cast leaves (`{0}` for `{"a": 0.1}` on Int64).
  - A struct of several fields, an empty struct or a nested struct fails
    with a SchemaError that names the cast type
    (`List(Struct({'a': Float32, 'b': Float32}))`), but only when a case's
    slice holds a non-null activity.
  - On any other column (Boolean, Date, Datetime, or a struct with a list
    field) the pattern always fails with its own type (`s1.py` to
    `s7.py`).
- **CJ1-9 Cast failures of the prefix and suffix filters.** A list pattern
  on a String column, or a str pattern on a Boolean column, fails its cast
  when the plan resolves, after the sort and group_by have found their
  columns (a missing case column still fails first). The message carries
  the plan resolved until the failure:
  - patterns before the failing one show their casts (`["1"]`, `[true]`,
    `["{1}"]`) and coerced slices (`(0 - n)`);
  - the failing pattern shows `.cast(List(String))` or
    `.cast(List(Boolean))`;
  - patterns after it show as built, with `(dyn int: 0 - dyn int:
    n.cast(Int64))` slices;
  - an empty pattern is `true`, and a leading `true` drops the outer
    parentheses;
  - leading equal patterns fold into one, and a single comparison prints
    its slice as `-n`.

  This was checked against `s8.py` to `s11.py` and a probe bank of 240
  calls.
- **CJ1-10 New domains.**
  - `scripts/polars_filter_cj_domain.py` builds on the CI domain, with
    typed activity columns in about half of the frames. It passes dict,
    list-of-dict and empty-dict bounds and anchors to the numeric,
    relative occurrence, between, case and paths performance filters,
    dict path items on typed columns, and lists mixing plain lists, lists
    of dicts and scalars. Its first bank (seed 2026111430, 300 frames,
    16,151 calls) differed in 607 calls; after CJ1-2 to CJ1-7, 0. Seed
    2026111432 (500 frames, 27,050 calls) differed in 7 (CJ1-5's AND/OR
    fold and the dict as written), then 0.
  - `scripts/polars_sequence_filter_cj_domain.py` builds on the CH
    sequence domain. In about 60% of the cases it puts dicts into the
    activity values of the value calls. Seed 2026111431 (600 frames, 8,076
    calls) differed in 39 calls, then 0. Seed 2026111433 (1,000 frames,
    12,976 calls) differed in 1 (CJ1-9), then 0.

Not taken (carried to CK):
- Int128 literals.
- A list whose first item is a struct and a later item a plain list
  (`[{"a": 1}, [-1], 5]`). Polars names the list item; the model names
  the scalar.
- `list[u64]` with a datetime struct field.
- A `bytes` anchor on a Null column (`cast(Int64).is_in([[120]])`; not
  generated).
- Items carried from CI: dicts and the comparison model on Duration,
  Time, Decimal and Int128 columns (declared), the `coerced_scalar_is_in`
  gaps, `list_literal` with wide ints after a float and in nested lists,
  `lit_supertype` of Int128 with temporal types, ints past the UInt64
  range as paths bounds, and `plan_text_at` when the failing leaf is
  inside a merged node.
- The items carried from CD.
